title: DISASTER OF A MACHINE
text:
HORRIBLE – DISASTER

I was really looking forward to getting this machine. The reviews were great and I really needed an upgrade from my Toshiba laptop. The Toshiba has been a great workhorse but is now dated. Over 5 years old and showing it. I have had good luck with Toshiba’s (have had 4) but felt it was time for a major upgrade in performance. This machine has many of the performance upgrades I felt would last for a few years – Good memory 1024 Gigs with an additional 256 G Solid State, BIG screen 17.3 inch, Upgraded graphics GeForce GTX970M w/3 GB vram, and 16 GB RAM. So I was really looking forward to getting this machine!!

There were a couple of issues I had to deal with in order to get the machine. I live in Central Mexico. Retired for the weather, cost of living and ease of travel. However, MSI like many companies will not ship to Mexico nor allow Amazon to ship to Mexico. So I had it sent to my son in the states.
He received it fine so I was looking forward to picking up the machine on our next visit. A couple of months after ordering the machine I visited my son and turned on the machine. It was beautiful and seemed to work great. I went on the internet and downloaded a couple of items before turning it off to return to Mexico.
FIRST ISSUE - On the way back to Mexico I turned the machine but was unable to get the Wi-Fi to connect.
Was a little frustrated but it worked OK at my son’s house so thought it was just an anomaly. Got home and the machine would still not connect to the Wi-Fi. Called customer service and ran thru several checks but no success. Had Customer Service send me a return and repair ticket RGA). Took the machine to DHL and sent it back to the repair facility in LA (shipping and ins cost $235.00).
A couple of weeks later the repair facility sent it back to my son. On my next trip North (Christmas Visit) I unpacked the machine confident that it was repaired. Powered it up and tried to log on to the internet.
SECOND ISSUE – Machine worked fine but NO WI-FI. The WI-FI didn’t even work the first time. Called Customer Service and they had me perform several fixes. Deleting the WI-FI driver and reinstalling corrected the issue. Great! However, when I turned the machine off and powered up the next day the WI-FI would not work again. Sensing the correction was the same as the prior day I deleted the WI-FI driver and reinstalled. WI-FI worked. Hmmmm! Not a good fix if I have to do this every time I want to use the machine. This reoccurred for a couple of days then….TA DA… the fix would not correct the issue (just knew I was living on borrowed time). Called Customer Service back and had them issue another RGA. Shipped back to LA (shipping and ins cost $70.00).

After a couple of weeks, the repair facility sent the #@& machine back to my son. I had him forward the machine to me in Mexico (total shipping, insurance and Mexico taxes cost $383.00). Received the machine, unpacked, connected the power cord and turned the machine on…er
THIRD ISSUE – The machine did not power up. There was a brief flicker when I pressed the power button but no success. After saying some very uncharacteristically foul words. I calmed down enough to get Customer Service back on the line to get an additional RGA. Sent the machine back to LA (total shipping, insurance cost $218.00, by this time the Dollar was stronger so cost me a little less in pesos).

After a couple of weeks, I had the repair facility send the %$#&*@#%# machine to some friend’s house in SoCal. They were on a trip and brought it back to me ($0 shipping cost).
Unpacked and turned on…SUCCESS! The machine powered up, WI-FI worked, screen is beautiful, sound is great, processor is very fast…wonderful.
FOURTH ISSUE - Used the machine 4 days and it powered down.. just turned off. Would not restart. The next day I tried to power up and it turned on for about 20 seconds. Called Customer Service (they know me pretty well by now) and they suggested it was probably the power cord. Not an easy thing to get as this machine does not use the same power cord that Toshiba and most of the laptops use. Had to have a new power cord sent from Guadalajara. Plugged in the new power cord and no success.
Called Customer Service and they said I could send it back but they would not replace the machine. Company policy is not to replace machines but to repair. They would also not reimburse me for shipping costs nor ship to Mexico. If I have a local repair facility open the machine to attempt to fix the problem, it will void the warranty.
It is a beautiful machine, a little heavy but looks good on the desk as long as I keep it dusted.

I have incurred $906.00 in shipping costs plus the cost of the machine and it still doesn’t work. How would you rate this machine or company? Too bad there are no MINUS stars. I have had excellent results with Amazon and all of its vendors, but not this time.

title: Maybe not the best option if you are a Mac user
text:
I have been using the mouse for several weeks on a MacBook Pro running Yosemite (OS X 10.10) and I haven't had disconnection problems but the mouse was almost unusable at first since the pointer movement wasn't smooth or accurate at all. This is my first wireless mouse so I'm used to the work with stander Apple and Logitech wired mice for the past 15 years.

The solution was to install the shareware USB Overdrive 3. It recognized the mouse even before restarting the computer (just turn the mouse off and on). Then you can modify not only the speed but also the acceleration, which seemed to fix the jerky movement of the mouse.

Scrolling up/down/left/right works well. The wheel is also a third button (which I usually configure on Expose/Mission Control to show my desktop).

The blue button doesn't work when clicked (I can't get USB Overdrive to pick it up) but the touch seems to work. You can swipe up and down on it and the movements are picked up as Key Tab and Key Delete but I haven't set them up properly. There is a shot vibration when you swipe to let you know the command was picked up.

I haven't tried installing the Microsoft IntelliMouse package since it is out dated and the installation fails in Yosemite.

The mouse feels well on the hand and is comfortable. The lack of driver support from Microsoft is the only reason why I'm giving it 3 stars.

title: Leegoal 2.5" to 3.5" Laptop IDE Hard Disk HDD Adapter sold by EPICDEALZ - careful, the title may throw you off
text:
Another review, for the Leegoal 2.5" to 3.5" Laptop IDE Hard Disk HDD Adapter sold by EPICDEALZ

I had a need to put a 2.5 IDE drive into a computer that used a 3.5 in IDE drive. This device was the easiest solution to that problem.

Packing... They are sent wrapped in a bubble wrap sheet, shipped in a shipping box.

Instructions.... This device is shipped with NO instructions however it is rather intuitive.

Condition.... They arrived in pretty good condition. One had the pins in a awkward angle inside the power plug and they had to be bent back in alignment so the power plug could be attached. No other problem found.

There are no power supplies as the power is taken from the power plug from the 3.5 in drive source.
This is a printed circuit with attachements for the connection to the 3.5 in hard drive connectors for data and power AND connector for the 2.5 in hard drive. Do understand this works from the 3.5 in cables to the 2.5 inch hard drive, not the reverse.

The printed circuit board is basic and simple and should be mounted where there is no bending or stress on the connectors as any force may do damage to the adaptor.

Connections are easy and fast. As soon as you are connected on both ends you should be ready to go, there is nothing else to do other than assembly. DO INSPECT ALL THE PINS BEFORE ASSEMBLY as you may receive on with misaligned pins. Simply bending them back in alignment should be all you need to do.
If you are making a connection that may be more or less PERMANENT, this should do the job, however, since the adapter is inexpensive and noting that the device is simply a printed circuit, I would recommend getting an extra one.

My View.... I had no problem with connection with this device after I had aligned the power pins. Worked perfectly as I needed and saved me a lot of time and money. I would recommend this adaptor if you need to replace a 3.5 in hard drive with a 2.5 in hard drive.

title: Nice out of the box BUT slow and buggy once you try to use the advertised features
text:
Right out of the box, I was unimpressed with this. It has so much promise, and the Ubiquiti team sells it very well. But it doesn't deliver. It feels like an open source hacker project that still ought to be in beta. I imagine that perhaps in 1-2 years it'll be ready for showtime but as with the other Ubiquiti products I've bought, they seem to release things before they are really ready for showtime. It works well until you try to configure it past the starting defaults.

Problems include:
* Feels underpowered. While it delivers on the bandwidth with the default settings, if you only try to implement a few of the features the throughput goes way down. I tried to implement some bandwidth controls / QoS and saw throughput go down from 100mbps to 30 as soon as that's implemented. So you undo that setting and it goes back up. A few other settings did the same thing. Ultimately, it appears that some of the IP and TCP offloading features have to be disabled as soon as you do advanced stuff and then the throughput becomes limited by the underpowered main processor.
* Each of the features seems to work by itself, but if you combine the wrong ones together, you'll have problems. The user forums have a fair number of situations where users and support persons are saying "oh, well you might have problems if you try to do both ___ and ___ at the same time".
* Are you kidding me? It doesn't even have a grounded plug. Just a cheap little power adapter. Feels like consumer grade stuff but they sell it as if it's powerful and as good as cisco.
* We started having a lot of extraordinarily frustrating problems with Google Drive / Gmail / Google services after installing this. Finally, many months later, I've realized the the problem is the Ubiquiti device. I found this forum post https://community.ubnt.com/t5/EdgeMAX/Problems-with-Google-Drive-quot-Trying-to-connect-quot-and-quot/td-p/1247106/page/2. This post exactly describes my problem and the company has no suggestions on how to fix it. Basically it's up to the user community to hack away and try to figure out the problem. Again, feels like a shoestring budget open source thing. Which is fine if that's what you thought you were signing up for--but this is not Cisco or Meraki or good stuff like that.
* The worst thing is that I've wasted ~15 hours over the past 8 months troubleshooting stupid problems caused by this that I didn't immediately realize were related to this cheap, buggy hardware. So, the TCO of this device is not $100 but $100 + 15 X (your hourly IT person's rate). Would have saved time and money by getting something more reliable (even if the alternative device claims less total features).

title: Fantastic performance, easy to setup and manage
text:
I've had a vareity of wireless routers over the years, from all the major brands - Linksys, Netgear, D-Link, etc. My home networking requirements are not especially complex, but I do have to main areas where there a lot of wired computers/devices, and need a good, fast connection between them - the living room, and my office area. To that end, I've tried several solutions - bridging between two routers, using a dedicated wireless to ethernet bridge in my office, powerline adapters, etc. Everything resulted in a connection that was either slow, or unreliable. I was almost to the point that I was ready to give up and just run Ethernet cable from the living room to the office, when by chance I saw the Google WiFi 3 pack was on sale. So I took the plunge and gave it a shot.

Setup is insanely easy - you just plug the the power into the first access point, connect it to your modem, and use the Android app to discover, configure it via QR code & confirm it's working. The app then instructs you to add the additional APs through your house one by one, discovering & joining them to the network. Once they're all up, you can test the connectivity between them to verify optimal placment.

Right away, I was able to easily bridge my living room and office area seamlessly, and the connection between the two environments is strong/fast. I also benefit from better coverage over the entire foot print of my house - very nice for when I'm outside and using a wireless device. In addition, several indepedent internet speed tests report slightly faster download/upload speeds than my old router setup - nothing over the top, it just seems to make better use of the bandwidth I'm paying for.

Also, I make use of features like DHCP reservations & port forwarding - these are all easy to setup and configure via the app. It's also nice to be able to manage screen time on the kids' devices a bit easier using the Family WiFi options to set time limits and enforce Google safesearch.

Overall, I'm very happy with Google wifi - it's easy to setup, has great coverage, and management is simple. I do wish configuration didn't rely on the app and could be done from a PC, but honestly, I'm never without my phone, so that's not that big of a deal.

THIS ONE IS TRULY INNOVATIVE, AND MINE HAS WORKED PERFECTLY SO FAR.  My previously owned remote controls were "device based" and you had to change from device to device to operate all of your equipment.  Let's say you have 5 devices, the old remote controls were better than 5 different remote controls and all of the clutter they caused.  AND it would take forever to program all of the functions that you want on a single remote control.  This Logitech Harmony 700 is "ACTIVITY BASED" and it was so easy to setup using my computer and the myharmony website. An example:  "DirecTV + Sound" as an activity does all of the following with the press of one button on the remote.  It turns on 3 devices; my TV and AV receiver, and the SAT receiver.  It sets the TV to the right input, it sets my sound amp to the right sound input, and device controls are for the DirecTV SAT receiver, and yet the sound and mute buttons affect my sound amplifier. It is wonderful.  I like the 700 better than the 650 because the batteries are more powerful and they are rechargeable.

title: WONDERFUL HEADSET
text:
These are great quality for the price. I definitely have brand loyalty. I am by no means a sound guru but I feel like they are good. The sound is clear with decent bass. Not booming mind you but good. It's user friendly which is great because my box was missing the manual. For those with the same issue here is how to use it.
Charge fully before first use. USB charging port is on the underside of the right ear with a light indicator.
There are three button controls on the back of the right ear.
Top is a plus sign for volume up
Middle is a circle which is the power on/off button, pause/play, answering phone calls.
Bottom is a minus for volume down.
To turn on or off hold down middle button for several seconds until you hear the ascending tones (power on) and descending tones (power off)
There is a sound indicating low battery. Typically 10 to 20 minutes before it dies.
It comes up as "uproar" on the Bluetooth menu.
You can use them while they are charging also though most companies don't suggest it. When you plug it in it'll turn the headset off so you'll have to turn it back on.
I believe on average it takes about one hour to fully charge, though don't quote me. I use mine heavily. Several hours throughout the day and fall asleep with them on all night. I usually forget to turn them off too and they last for about 48 hours this way on one charge which is saying something. They are on the majority of a 24 hour period.
I hope this was helpful to somebody.

title: Very unreliable
text:
When they work, they're really great. The problem? They fail all of the time.

Hardware:
1-2 devices have a hardware failure every year and need to be replaced, sometimes but not always covered by warranty. Even if it's covered by warranty, you'll spend 2-4 hours waiting to get a hold of someone at SmartHome. You'll then be without a light switch for 4-5 days as it ships to you. And then you get to deal with rewiring a 120V switch or outlet. If you're handy, then it's just a pain in the ass. If you're paying someone to install these for you, that really sucks.

Software:
Their software is incomprehensible to me, which is sad given that I work in technology and some degree of actual programming experience. The switches seem to lose their programming randomly and need to be reprogrammed. This can easily take 2-3 hours for my home with ~18 switches as the switches must not only be programmed to work with each other, but also the Insteon Hub app on your phone. I usually have to do this 1-2 times a year. The time-savings from being able to turn off all of the lights in my house from a single switch are nice, but this routine hassle is getting old.

Don't expect to be able to rent your home to someone with these switches installed. They will drive you and your tenant crazy.

title: Amplified TV Antenna.
text: Had problems, but customer service was great and got me a replacement very promptly.  New one works great.  Picks up stations like crazy.  Two very important points to prospective buyers:  1:  There is absolutely no indication which way the antenna is pointing.  This is terrible when trying to point the antenna for a particular station you want to watch.  I have to just go outside and look, go in and push a direction button (no way to tell which one to push) and go out to see what happened.  Very frustrating,  2:  If the only way you can program stations on your TV is "auto program"  you will only get nearby stations or the stations the antenna is pointing toward.  This problem applies to ANY directional TV antenna, however.  You should be aware of this common problem with many TV sets, i.e. the inability to add channels to your list manually.  All that said, you will not get a better antenna for this price.

title: Best TV Decision I Could Make
text: Installed this antenna on my rooftop this week.  It has surpassed my expectations in its ability to receive digital channels.  My house is located between Chicago and Milwaukee, I have lots of large tall trees nearby as well as taller houses, and this antenna still picks up over 50 channels.  I have pointed it in the direction of where most of the Milwaukee TV transmitters are, and to my surprise, the antenna not only picks up the Milwaukee channels great, but also picks up the Chicago stations when it is not pointed in their direction.  I highly recommend this product.  The difficult part of the installation is running the coaxial wires through the walls and floor of the house.  The stand for the antenna is sold separately.  The antenna comes with a decent length of coaxial cable included, but in my case I needed 100 feet of coaxial cable so I ordered that separately as well.  I use Roku devices in conjunction with the HD antenna to provide my household with a massive array of free quality television.  I am very happy with this antenna.

title: HDMI to Component converter has problems with my Comcast cable box.
text:
I am using a Slingbox 500 with an older Comcast cable box that has the component outputs required for Slingbox. The newer Comcast boxes do not have component outputs. Before replacing my Comcast box I decided to try the HDMI to component converter with my existing Comcast box to see if it would work. The converter has one HDMI input, one HDMI output and component outputs. It is powered through a USB port on either the Comcast box or the Slingbox.

Once I had the units all hooked up, the TV and the Slingbox stream (as viewed on my Ipad) would periodically go blank for a few seconds and then recover. Thinking it might be the interaction between the converter and the Slingbox, I disconnected the component cables between the converter and the Slingbox and the periodic blank outs continued. At this point the connection was HDMI from the Comcast box to the converter, and HDMI from the converter to the TV. So, with the Slingbox out of the picture, I have to conclude that the converter is at fault. I will try a different brand of converter to determine if there is any solution at all Comcast's disappointing upgrade.

title: So far, so ok. Not good, just ok.
text:
(UPDATE) 10/7/2016:

I ended up returning my FireTV because it was just too frustrating to deal with. But a year later one of my friends has purchased the FireTV and he let me put it through it's paces. I have to say, it's better, a lot better. It's actually quite good. It's still in your face with Prime stuff, but all of the issues I had with mine seem to have been resolved. The sound is great for ALL apps and content, not just Prime and everything comes across the A/V receiver as 5.1. The video quality is fantastic for all apps and content. I had issues with video not being anywhere close to how it should be with jagged edges and blurriness. This has been fixed too. Now the video quality is perfect and 4K content looks amazing. It also seems that Alexa has been drastically improved and is a lot better at recognizing what i'm saying and also provides results from other apps and content outside of Prime! Excellent! The issues I had with the remote have also been resolved. The remote is now responsive and doesn't require me to press the keys multiple times. I put it through a barrage of tests. Opening and closing apps. Starting and stopping tv shows, movies, navigating around the UI, voice searches, etc... There was no locking up like I experienced previously, there were no reboots in the middle of watching content like I experienced previously. It was smooth, responsive and free of all of the frustrating buggy antics that forced me to return my unit. It's so good now that i'm seriously considering repurchasing the FireTV. Kudos to Amazon for resolving all of the issues I faced a year ago, you've made a believer out of me and I just might be reordering very soon.

(UPDATE) 10/9/2015:

I will now be sending my Fire TV back and pre-order a Roku 4. So far it's been ok, but last night I put it through it's paces watching multiple shows and movies, and doing some games. I had nothing but problems. Freezing, remote control stopped working, at one point it took 4 minutes for a movie on Netflix to start, then once it started it kept freezing up. The box even rebooted itself during a TV show I was watching. Problem after problem after problem. It then becomes a frustrating experience instead of an enjoyable one. And the constant barrage of Prime content in my face is getting really annoying. I love Prime, I've been a Prime member for about 3 years now, but come on. Tone it down a little. The sound is horrendous, the picture quality for 4K material is probably worse than a 1080p feed. It's got so many problems that I just can't hang on and wait for the developers to get these problems fixed with a software update, and I don't have much confidence that when they do it won't create more problems. It is such a shame because it has so much potential, but you can definitely tell that bad decisions were made and corners were cut for the sake of market placement. I'm a software developer and I would be ashamed of myself if I produced software this buggy. I hope that when Amazon begins development on generation 3 that they learn from the horrific mistakes they made with this generation and produce something that both the company and the consumer can be proud of. This is far from that. This is such a let down. I am a huge Amazon fan. I spend thousands a year on products. I love the Prime offerings. I try to get as much of the things I need from Amazon, especially around the holidays and this is just a kick in the teeth. When my Fire TV was delivered they should have just sent over an Amazon representative with it to throw it at me, give me the finger and kick me in the jumblies.

I received my new Fire TV yesterday and hooked it up last night. For my setup I ran the HDMI cable directly to my TV into an HDCP 2.2 port as my A/V receiver does not have 4K pass through, only 1080p, but my 4K TV is setup to send the sound to my A/V receiver.

Setup was simple, I didn't have any issues. It booted, checked for updates, downloaded and installed an update, rebooted, checked again then updated the remote, then it was ready to go. The whole thing took about 5 minutes. Seems reasonable to me.

It streamed 4K to my TV validated by my TV displaying 4K input. It does seem that the 4K stream coming from the Fire TV is overly compressed. It seems a bit jittery. I have both the Netflix app and the Amazon Prime app on the TV and the video from those apps is better than the video coming from the Fire TV. One star off for this. I'm hoping that a firmware upgrade with fix this in the very near future (within 30 days or I will return).

I am also experiencing the Dolby issue with apps other than Amazon Prime. All sound outside of Amazon Prime is 2-channel stereo. Another star off for this. Although I do now see that Amazon has acknowledged this issue and will be issuing an update later this month to fix.

The menu's are just ok. It's quite obvious that Amazon has pushed their ecosystem right to the front in the UI. But I don't blame them. Apple does the same with their music and video apps at the top of the UI, while getting to Netflix and other apps requires scrolling down. But in the Fire TV it's more "In your face" with the design.

So far so good. Not amazing, but good. I'll update the review in a couple of days after I've had the chance to delve in to all of the features.

P.s. The price has dropped from $99 to $79. There is no need to scream and yell at Amazon reps and threaten to return and reorder the product to get the $20 difference refunded. Just go to the contact us page (search contact in Amazon for a link), enter your info, start a chat, request a difference refund and give the rep the order number. You'll get your refund.

(UPDATE): Not sure what Amazon is playing at, but now the price is back at $99. I was lucky, I jumped on my request for the $20 refund and received it while the price was showing at $79. Now apparently customers are being told there was no price drop. This whole thing smells fishy to me. I'll agree with a few other reviewers who question why the audio bug was not discovered before production release. Now I'm not buying the story. It's virtually impossible for not even one person who beta tested to not have a surround sound system and to realize that it does not produce 5.1 for anything but Amazon Prime content? I'm just not buying it. This had to be an executive decision to limit 5.1 audio to Amazon Prime making it seem as though Amazon Prime was superior to Netflix to try to entice customers to switch from Netflix to Prime. Now it's backfired and everyone responsible at Amazon is running around with their hands in the air after the plethora of bad reviews have rolled in. For the first time I am really disappointed with Amazon. I will hang on to my Fire TV for the 30 day return window and test the bejesus out of it. But if the issues are not fixed within that timeframe, I'm sending it back. Amazon has done an absolutely horrible job at not only releasing a product that is clearly not ready for production use, but also jerking customers around with the price changes that have happened today and giving vague responses to issues that customers have detailed.

Another star off for the bad customer relation behavior.

(UPDATE 2): After tinkering for a couple of days now it's not a bad little streamer. However I cannot raise my rating yet.

Problems:

1) 5.1 DD does not work for anything other than Amazon Prime. Some people have reported this, some people have reported that it only affects Netflix, but in my case it affects everything except Amazon Prime.

2) Hard to find UHD in Amazon Prime. This is a strange one because the Prime app on my Smart TV allows a search for UHD or Ultra HD and shows all of the UHD movies and shows. On the Fire TV it does not. There is no category on my Fire TV for UHD titles. I have read that some people are seeing this category but i'm not. Some people are saying it comes and goes, sometimes it's there sometimes it's not. I haven't seen it once.

3) Remote sometimes unresponsive. Sometimes I will have to press the buttons on my remote multiple times for it to work.

4) Volume for all apps is very low. I generally have my A/V receiver set to between 50 and 60 for the volume for all of my devices, PlayStation, Apple TV, BluRay player, SAT box, and they all have good sound. I have to crank up my A/V receiver to almost 80 to get decent volume out of the Fire TV.

5) Overly crowded UI with Prime content. I get that Amazon wants to push their Prime ecosystem but it's a bit much. You're constantly bombarded with Amazon stuff.

6) While the Alexa voice search is good, it's limited and obviously geared towards Prime content. I wish Alexa would show you search results from whatever apps I choose, even if they forced it to search Prime, allow it to search say Netflix and other apps too.

7) Video quality not as good as it should be. It seems compressed with both 1080p and 2160p feeds getting jittery. My internet connection is very fast and I do not have this problem on my Apple TV and with the Prime and Netflix apps on my Smart TV. In fact the picture on the Prime app on my Smart TV is amazing, especially with 4K content, it's fantastic. But on the Fire TV it gets blurry at times and has trouble when there is a lot of action going on. Same company right? Both my Smart TV and this Fire TV box are connected to the same WiFi network, and they are right next to each other, and my WiFi router is in the same entertainment centre as my FireTV.

PROS:

1) Very fast UI. The interface is surprisingly fast. Remember that the UI is HTML5 so it relies on web calls to show content. If your internet connection is slow this will slow the UI. Mine is fast FiOS so the interface is snappy coupled with a fast processor it's quite fast.

2) Easy setup. The setup for me was extremely easy. Plugged it in, waited a few seconds for it to boot, setup the WiFi network connection, it did an update, rebooted, did another update, rebooted and it was ready to go. The entire setup process took approx. 5 minutes.

3) Small footprint. The unit is tiny, smaller than my Apple TV (3rd Gen).

4) Alexa seems to be pretty good understanding my commands. I haven't had an issue with it recognizing what i'm saying. It's also pretty responsive, but again this would rely on the speed of your internet connection I would assume as Alexa is cloud based.

Thoughts so far:

While it's not terrible, I feel that it was released prematurely. I'm still sticking to my thought that something fishy is going on with the issues and the price changes that happened yesterday. But, this unit has great potential. The hardware is there, it just needs the software. In this world of TV streamers such as Apple TV, Chromecast, Roku and others you can't be half-assed about releasing a product, there is just too much competition out there. I'm an avid Apple fan and 99% of my content is in the Apple ecosystem. But Apple has disappointed at least me, maybe others, by announcing a new TV box with no 4K support when all of the other players are releasing 4K streamers this year. This is the only reason I moved to the Fire TV because I wanted the 4K features. I've waited for Apple to release a new box and it should have had 4K on it. But i'll just keep my 3rd Gen Apple TV now until the Apple does something to support 4K on theirs. The ridiculous part about that is that they announced that the new phones would record in 4K and yet they release an Apple TV that you will not be able to play those 4K videos on! Silly. Bu I digress, this is not an Apple review. Amazon needs to step up and step up quickly to get the issues resolved. I hope they do. I hope that the disappointment that I have in Amazon for the first time will be remedied.

Doesn't seem strange that there are so many 5 star reviews from people that have this Fire TV as their only review? Food for thought...

title: Follow This Procedure To Clone Your Existing Properly & You'll Love The Samsung 970
text:
I purchased the 1TB 970 so I could upgrade the boot drive in a Lenovo Flex 5 1570. I had difficulty getting the existing (512GB) NVMe SSD cloned and bootable, but once I cloned it to an external USB 2.5" SSD drive, then restored it to the now-installed 970, everything worked perfectly.

I own multiple backup and cloning software programs, but none would yield the desired results and I was getting really frustrated. Then, the director of IT at my company told me to use the free version of MiniTool Partition Wizard. I downloaded it and it quickly cloned the original boot SSD to my external USB SSD drive. I then installed the 970 and restored the clone to the 970. I then shut the system down, disconnected the external SSD and booted to the 970. It booted flawlessly. I did have to re-authenticate Windows, but it was almost painless, unlike the old days.

I now have bought a 2TB version of the 970 and will be doing the exact same procedure to clone the 1TB to the new 2TB 970.

BTW, if you've never had an NVMe SSD, be prepared for it to run hot. Do everything you can to keep it cool, though, and you'll be really amazed by the speed --- especially the speed with which your computer boots into Windows. Schwing, indeed.

I highly recommend the Samsung 970 family of NVMe SSDs.

title: Fragile, But Functional.
text:
This gadget gets the job done. As expected, it's a perfect fit for the PS4 controller and will not fit any other type of controller. It is used with an 8 inch HP tablet and the suction cup holds the flat back of the tablet perfectly. I'm not sure how well it would work if the tablet or phone had a textured backing or was in a case.

I knocked off a star because this thing is fragile. The first one I received was broken-- the round discs that hold the clamping arm were both snapped off during shipping, and since they function to hold the clamp together and act as hinges for the clamping arm, they're pretty vital to functionality of the gadget and they're irreparable, even with glue. They were broken into several tiny pieces. Amazon accepted it as a return and replaced the item, and the second one arrived intact. Having seen the inside of the gadget though, I now know those hinges are a weak point and if the mount ever gets dropped or bumped, there's a good chance of it breaking. I also believe this item is fairly overpriced, given that it is a small piece of molded plastic with a couple small screws and a suction cup. title: thumbs up from Linux user
text:
I'll start with what I found to be the difference between the neo and the other models. I thought the only real difference was NFC in the neo. But I found out the ccid feature that only the neo has is really cool. With the neo you can use oath-totp which is what google authenticator uses. So you can use this instead of google authenticator. You can scan the key with an android phones NFC and it will show you the pins. You can also plug it into the computer and use a yubico ( open source ) app to display the pins. But it uses the ccid (when you get the key use the neo manager and make sure ccid is enabled) smart card function to communicate with the key, so you have to have the neo to do it. The standard key will do oauth- totp but it will use one of the two slots, so you could only use it with two sites. If you want to use oath-totp (google authenticator) and you probably do the neo is the only one for you.
The yubico one time password I have used on absolutely nothing. I'm not even using either one of the slots. I ended up (so far) just using the oath-top and fido U2F. Which doesn't use either other the config slots. When something wants to use the U2F the key just changes states seamlessly. Since more sites support google authenticator than anything else I use that on most site. It's nice having it on the key instead of the phone. I left my phone at the house, but wanted to locate it to make sure it was there. I barrowed a phone installed the yuico authenticator app and was able to log into google. If I was using the the google authenticator I would not be able to login on anything with out the phone.
The fido U2F I'm only using on google and dropbox, as the other sites I use don't support it YET. But it works flawlessly, And I got it so I can log into my desktop with it (Linux Mint).
The difference between the neo and the edge is the edge is a regular yubikey with fido U2F. You'd only need it if you want to use the standard otp function and U2F but didn't want NFC or oath-totp. You'll have to check you sites you want to secure to see if that is a good scenario for you.
Now I'll talk about Linux and the yubikey. When I first heard about them I didn't know they had open sourced all there work. I would have gotten one much sooner If I'd know that. But that means it works freaking great in Linux. There's a repository for Ubuntu (works fine with Mint) "sudo add-apt-repository ppa:yubico/stable". After that all the utilities to configure it or use the authenticator are easy as anything else to install. I hear there's a pip repository for it too. They seem to have written every thing in python.
I've seen some people complaining about using FIDO keys in Linux. They work fine you have to make a udev rule for the key. The details are on yubico's gethub page https://github.com/Yubico/libu2f-host/blob/master/70-u2f.rules it take 30 seconds to copy and paste the file. After that putting in the repo installing everything that came up in the package manager when I searched for yubico, I was completely set up for way more than I even thought I'd be. The U2F worked on google and dropbox with zero problems, I didn't even install the chrome extension for it.
Desktop login was so simple. I had to install a couple of U2F packages run a utility to generate a key file, and and a few line in a couple /etc/udev/pam.d/files. Here's the guide I used http://www.mikejonesey.co.uk/security/2fa/linux-desktop-2fa-with-pam-u2f . I now have it so when I login to the command line, the GUI desktop, or unlocking the screen saver it needs to factor with my password and the FIDO key. But if I'm logged in I can run root commands with only a touch of the key, instead of a password. But you can configure it anyway you like.

title: HUGE disappointment with product and customer service is atrocious
text:
Update on 4/1/17

A piece of OUTRAGEOUSLY overpriced junk. This afternoon, for absolutely no reason, the touchscreen stopped working. Even after a call to customer service it wouldn't reboot and work. New Kindle due to be delivered tomorrow but this will be the third Kindle since Christmas. The most expensive e-reader anywhere has turned out to be an unreliable piece of junk. I may end up going back to my seven year-old Kindle 2nd Generation. Can't believe the outrageous price for the most unreliable electronic device I've ever owned.

I'm a firm believer in "if it ain't broke don't fix it" and should have kept to that before asking for the most expensive Kindle for a Christmas gift. My seven year-old Kindle 2nd generation still works fine but I am afraid that I will go to start it and find it's no longer functional. Problems started immediately and after spending HOURS on the phone and four disconnects from live chat I was ready to pitch everything into the street.
1. Customer service (and I use the term loosely) is absolutely useless. My first call and first wasted hour was with a difficult to understand male who kept referring to my Kindle Fire. After the fifth time I was screaming at him that I was calling about an Oasis. Apparently he only had the manual for the Fire.
2. No one was able to tell me why my battery was used up twice as fast as my old Kindle. I finally took a shot and put it in airplane mode and it slowed down, NO thanks to customer service.
3. I wanted 3G because I wanted to be sure I have access to books when I stay with friends who don't have WiFi. The 3G on the Oasis is slower than the 2nd generation.
4. I don't see a huge difference in the fonts and readability in the Oasis. Not needing a book light is an improvement but I'm not sure it's worth $400.
5. The home page is far more confusing than the old device. That worked fine and I fail to see how having to go from "all" to "downloaded" is an improvement. Samples are jumbled up with books.
6. I wanted physical page turn buttons but the screen is ultra-sensitive and I'm frequently having to go back.
7. It's lightweight and will probably be a little easier to travel with.

All-in-all I see nothing to recommend the Oasis and given the absolutely arrogant and useless customer service I can't recommend this product and won't be buying an Echo any time soon. Amazon needs to bring its call center back to the USA and staff it with individuals who are polite, knowledgeable and SPEAK ENGLISH!

title: Amazon Fire TV is the best choice, but this one is not great. Get the stick or a refurbished box.
text:
Updated my review down to 2 stars. I found out that ATMOS does not reliably work with my receiver, it also does switches on the receiver like previous versions and the remote went down in quality. It was already not a great upgrade from the 2nd generation Fire TV box but even the Amazon Fire TV stick is a better choice. I am returning it because I expect a software update cannot fix this, especially not the remote.

Long time Cord cutter here. We had been wanting to dump cable for some time but were scared to leave our comfort zone. Since we are Prime members, we finally decided to give Amazon Fire TV a shot. All our TV's have now a Fire TV, this is the fourth Fire TV I bought in three years now and we'll never go back to cable!

PROS:

Ridiculously easy to set up and small form factor which takes up very little space.

Simple remote (and a free app so you can turn your cell or tablet into a remote).

No buffering issues have yet come up (although that may be because I have a very strong internet connection).

Seamless interaction with our Prime Video account and Amazon Music, across all devices. For example, if I download a movie from Prime on my
tablet, watch some of it during my commute - when I get home and turn on Fire TV, I can pick up right where I left off from my tablet...seamlessly
without having to manually sync.

Comes with thousands of channels/apps loaded including all of the the major services we use.

Can be used for games, use separate Bluetooth controller for a better experience.

The voice command feature is outstanding. Speak the name of a show or movie and be taken instantly to it, with multiple options for buying,
renting or just viewing for free if available. I've never been a big voice command user with other devices but this one works so well that using it has already become a habit.

Using the Amazon Photos app you can instantly upload all of your digital photos from your phone or tablet to your Fire TV for large screen viewing of your photos.

CONS: No way to customize the home screen layout, other than setting favorites on apps.

OVERALL: I'm kicking myself for not doing this sooner. Since we use Prime and Amazon Music, its a no-brainer for us to use the Fire TV. Everything syncs automatically and transfers from device to device seamlessly.

COMPARED to the Fire TV stick and previous Fire TV box:

I see this as the successor of the Fire TV stick and not the Fire TV box because it lacks a microSD card slot, USB and Ethernet port (2nd generation Fire TV box removed optical port already).

It is a bit faster than the stick (not as fast as the Fire TV box, but still more responsive than for example an Apple TV), it supports 4K 60FPS with HDR and Dolby Atmos sound (although it did not work with my Yahama Amplifier, I had to disable Dolby altogether to get sound).

The remote with Alexa microphone, is not the same great quality as the previous versions, there is a seam on both sides when closed, the skin of your hand will come in between it and hurts when pressing a button.

A power adaptor is bundled, you don't need the adaptor if the USB of your TV provides enough power, I ignored the low-power warnings and it works just fine.

If you miss the USB port or SD slot you can still use an OTG adaptor https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00CXAC1ZW/ or get the refurbished old version (without HDR and Dolby Atmos)

For Ethernet you can get this adapter [[ASIN:B074TC662N Amazon Ethernet Adapter for Amazon Fire TV Devices]]

Gamers can better buy the previous version or wait till there is a new desktop model, this one is a quite a bit slower while gaming.

If you are a first-time cord-cutter, considering cord-cutting or new to streaming TV services, here are a few things to keep in mind:

Make sure you really take the time to do research and due-diligence on cord-cutting. Just google "cord cutting" to get started with several good articles. I'm seeing a lot of 1 and 2 star reviewers who seemed surprised that they actually have to pay for things like Netflix, Hulu, etc. Fire TV (and all of the other streaming services like Roku, Apple TV, etc.) do not just give you free access to all content. They allow you to pick and choose what you want to watch and pay for as opposed to making you pay a big fee for a huge amount of channels you will never watch. If you do it right, you'll have access to the content you want for a substantial savings over what you were paying with cable.
Make sure you have a strong (and fast) internet connection. This is very important. We dumped our cable company in its entirety (including internet service) and upgraded to a faster dedicated line internet service with another company. We have up to six devices simultaneously streaming at any given time in our house and our internet service can handle all of that as well as the streaming Fire TV. So make sure yours can as well. If you're not sure, call your internet service provider, tell them you are planning to switch to streaming television and ask them about your current speeds.

Some apps require a cable subscription. You can purchase a streaming service like Sling which will bundle several of the channels you likely want but you may find yourself unable to access certain apps. For now password sharing with one of your friends may solve that problem but I suspect its only a matter of time before that loophole gets closed. So do your research and make sure you can access the channels you want.

Give yourself time to adjust to the new interface. It took some getting used to when I lost my ability to surf the cable channel guide. But the fact is, I'm no longer wasting large chunks of time mindlessly surfing the guide. Rather than surf, I'm turning to specific apps to watch specific programs. Its liberating in a way that I didn't expect. Besides, I can now surf all of the Amazon Prime content by simply using the voice command on the remote.

To see if your App or channel is available you can look here https://www.amazon.com/Fire-TV-Apps-All-Models/b?node=10208590011

If you want to install kodi look at the questions section, I did put a walkthrough there.

Comparison of the full specifications between all models is here: https://developer.amazon.com/docs/fire-tv/device-specifications.html

title: Don't ever even bother buying this if you care for your mental health.
text:
I got this SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive as a black Friday deal and if not the end, it was the midst of January when I was able to receive it. At first I liked having a small sized storage unit with my important files, windows/Linux installations, useful tools etc . that I can carry on me all the time.

If it's only tests you're wondering, the products read/write speeds seem excellent.
Well, don't be fooled.

The moment you start writing data more than a few hundred megabytes, the disk starts getting extremely hot.
So hot that when you eject it you can't even hold it. And at that moment your computer starts ejecting/inserting the usb to protect itself.

That results in partial transfers, incomplete transfers and an enriched vocabulary for you. If I can't keep it plugged in more than 60 seconds when I'm transferring data, what's the meaning of buying this? I tried it on multiple operating systems and they all resulted the same. Transfer speed goes up to 100mb for 1-2 seconds then quickly starts dropping and suddenly your operating system tells you that the drive has been removed! Then inserted, removed, inserted, removed. It's like Sandisk made this product to make you hate them or to torment you.

Right now I'm trying to copy 12GB worth of files to the usb disk. Every 700-800MB's or so I have to pause the transfer and let it cool of for about 30 secs before I can continue .

title: Awesome Quality at Great Price
text:
I was thoroughly impressed with the Tozo T10. The packaging was incredible, the build quality is top notch, and an amazing set of features for the price even if the price was twice as high. Wireless charging, IPX8 waterproofing, high quality 8mm sound driver, and bluetooth v5.0 are just a few of the high end features the T10's have to offer.

Pairing them with my phone was too easy. All you have to do is take them out of the charging case and they are ready for pairing( just a quick note make sure you choose TOZO-T10-R, the right earbud is the primary). The bluetooth v5.0 mean they have a stronger connection and longer distance. I can leave them in my backpack and I am still connected up to 30 feet away. The clarity of the highs and the richness of the bass are of the quality level of the highest end earbuds. I have personally taken these into the shower, I wasn't actually showering at the time, both of the earbuds and the case itself are extremely water resistance. I was pleasantly surprised to find that I could use my T10s for a little over four hours and the charging case is good for four full recharges of the earbuds. Finally, I have to say the Qi wireless chargeable case is very handy. I can set my phone and earbud case on my Qi charging pad and I'm good to go. If you have never used wireless charging, you need to. All in all for the price I could not find a better earbud on the market.

title: Great sound, very cute!  Only 3" x 3"
text:
I use this speaker to pair with my iPad when watching movies or shows...I love how compact it is!

It is an equilateral triangle, with each side of the triangular sides measuring 3". It is also 3" wide (from left to right side).

It comes with a small drawstring pouch to carry it in, as well as a charging cord. I should mention, the sound only comes out of the front panel -- it can be hard to tell from the picture, but it's not projecting sound out the back as well -- the back side is solid.

I think it holds its battery life pretty well -- longer than an iPad, at least! It will last for at least 3-4 hours, probably longer, though I haven't pushed it until it stops yet. Charges in less time than any of the devices I'm using it with, too, so that should never be an issue! (Its charging cord is the common micro USB kind, which is nice, since most people probably have several of those already from old Bluetooth headsets, kindles, etc...)

It pairs quickly and easily via Bluetooth -- I tried it with both my phone and iPad, and had absolutely no problems. It does indeed allow you to take calls from it, turning it into a speaker phone, which can be very handy at work.

The sound is great, especially for such a small speaker...it is surprisingly loud and clear. To me it doesn't sound at all "tinny" or make vibrating sounds like other small speakers I've used. You can control the volume from your phone or other device, or on the left side of the speaker itself (you can also answer the phone on the same side of the speaker).

It has a 3.5 mm headphone jack, which I use sometimes with a male-to-male 3.5 mm cord to hook it up to my PC, or if I'm connecting it to a device that Bluetooth isn't on, like my older iPod.

Overall, I am super pleased with the Roar Mini...it's very cute, has great sound, and is very easy to use!

title: SET IT and FORGET IT HDTV Antenna if you don't have mountains or buildings blocking direct line of site!
text:
The previous TV antenna that I had on the roof was a ClearStream 4 Indoor/Outdoor HDTV Antenna that was purchased several years ago at a local Best Buy. I bought it because it looked compact, and was made specifically for HD television reception vs. my old analog antenna. It did improve reception, and I wound up getting more channels in the Los Angeles metropolitan area (I’m in Orange County CA). The only problem that I had was with two channels. If the antenna was a little too far to the right I would get channel 7 KABC coming in fine, but then channel 4 KNBC would come in wonky/pixelated or not at all. The opposite would occur if I turned the antenna a little too far to the left. Channel 4 KNBC would come in fine, and then channel 7 KABC would be the problematic one. I could never find the sweet spot. Mount Wilson, which is located in Los Angeles County is where all of the television transmitters for the LA metro area are placed (excluding channel 24 KVCR). It is about 65 miles away. I thought, hey this is a pricey fancy HD antenna, with a 70 mile range, so I guess I’m screwed if even this antenna can’t get these two stations to come through at the same time. I even bought an amplifier and it didn’t really help.

I was doing some work on the roof, so I decided to check if there were better antennas out there now. I wanted to purchase a new antenna with a more robust range than the ClearStream 4. I found the Lava Omnipro HD-8008 Omni-Directional HDTV Antenna. I researched the antenna online, and found that it is supposed to have a 125 mile range. I thought it would be nice to be able to set the antenna and forget it. I did just that. After installing the new antenna on the roof, and connecting the antenna to the included power inserter, and the power inserter to the TV, I did a rescan on the Phillips 47 inch TV in the living room, and was able to get more channels, and their sub-channels. Most of the new channels and sub-channels are foreign language such as Spanish, Vietnamese, and Korean. So, it’s definitely receiving the stations with transmitters on Mount Wilson. Thus it has a 65 mile range for sure.

I now get channel 7 KABC and channel 4 KNBC at the same time without any pixelation problems. If your television has a really good tuner you will be able to pick up more channels with the antenna. I have a smaller Vizio model in one of the bedrooms, and it was able to pick up channel 6 KSFV-CD.

The antenna was easy to install, but to be honest it feels cheap like if the wind were to knock it down it would break too easily. I would recommend installing it in a very overly secure manner if you are placing it outside vs in your attic. My old antenna pole was a bit wonky, so I purchased an extra clamp to make sure the wind would not tip it over.

My main gripes about the Omnipro HD-8008 Omni-Directional HDTV Antenna are that it:
A. Feels cheap like it will easily break.
B. It’s a white color, and normally white plastic discolors, and turns into a burnt brown/yellow. It claims to have an anti-UV coating, but only time will tell. If it does turn brown/yellow quickly, I will definitely lower my rating. I would have preferred that the antenna be a black color.

If you don’t have mountains or tall buildings blocking your line of site, I would recommend the Lava Omnipro HD-8008 Omni-Directional HDTV Antenna so that you can set it and forget vs. having to deal with another brand, which would require you to get back up on your roof and tweak the direction or having to deal with a switch near your TV that rotates the TV antenna for you, and then having to worry about moving parts breaking.

PS. You may want to get some Rust-Oleum Never Wet Multi-Surface Spray to help minimize rain related interference.

title: You won't find a better tablet for under $200 than the Hi10 Plus.
text:
The build quality is impressive. The tablet feels like a premium product. The 1080p screen is gorgeous and bright. I keep the backlight setting at its darkest and the screen still is bright and colorful. The best part of the screen though in my opinion is the aspect ratio of 3:2. This is an ideal ratio for a screen this size as it makes it much more comfortable to hold with one hand than a typical 16:9 screen. The speakers are what you would expect from a tablet but I would say they are just as good as the speakers on my wife's iPad Air. 

Performance is solid for typical everyday use. The Atom Cherry Trail Z8350 processor along with a generous 4GB of RAM ensures that web browsing, Office work and playing games all work smoothly. Of course you cannot play demanding games like Forza Horizon 3 on it but you can play the latest Asphalt Xtreme game with no problem. 

Battery life has been excellent and I typically get 8-10 hours of use from each charge.

The tablet comes with both Android 5.1 as well as Windows 10. I don't use Android too often. Perhaps if it was the newest version of Android I would be more interested. I primarily use Windows 10. Out of the box Windows will need a lot of updates. Be patient and install them all as you will see an incredible performance gain once all the OS and chipset drivers have been installed.

As I use the tablet more I will update this review with any new information or issues. This is a fantastic buy at $199.

My only "con" right now is that there is a little air bubble near the edge of the screen on the bezel. This does not impact the screen in any way but to be thorough I wanted to mention it.

title: DSLRDashboard and a tip to be able to keep your 3G/4G active during use!
text:
I bought this to connect qDSLRDashboard to a canon camera (7DmkII in my case) to allow clients to see their pictures as they're taken. For the price, it's absolutely great. Having said that, however, if I were going to run this in a "real" studio environment, I'd probably fork over the $$$ for an actual CamRanger because of the more professional look and feel to the software. Thankfully, this setup will more than serve my purpose for 1/10 the price.

To do it yourself, just follow the instructions at qDSLRDashboard or, alternately, DSLRController if you're an android user. Be careful - each app has its own firmware and they are not compatible with each other. I chose DSLRDashboard because of the iOS, Android, Mac and PC apps. It gives me a lot of flexibility.

Btw, the PC and Mac apps are free. The iOS and Android are about $10. Seriously, folks, if you get this working and use it (even on the PC or a Mac), buy one of the mobile apps just to support the developer. He's obviously earned it with the effort that has gone into this! It took a bit of tinkering and trial and error, but once working, it works very well. Here are a few hints to help the process...

1) once you've flashed the new firmware and connected your pc to the TP-Link wifi, click the NETWORK button to connect in DSLRDashboard. I kept clicking the canon button to connect which didn't work. Click network and it should connect.

2) if you are using the mobile app and make any changes to the TP Link router for any reason (settings, etc), you should probably kill the app and restart it to avoid errors and the such.

3) I read a number of complaints about not being able to attach the TP to your hot shoe. I went down to Ace hardware and bought a 1/4-20 receiver, drilled a 3/8" hole in the TP bottom plate (it comes off easily to reveal the battery), and pushed the receiver through the hole. Just for overkill, I also cut off the edges of the receiver to fit inside the battery panel grooves so that it won't rotate when tightening and loosening. Now, I have a 1/4-20 receiver sticking out the bottom that I can use for a hot shoe ball joint adapter. See pics (I left a second receiver in the pic to show the whole piece)...

4) my biggest issue was having to reconnect my phone to wifi (and therefore disconnect from the TP) to post or send a photo (or even check email for that matter). As it turns out, you can get an iPhone to keep its cell connection active while connected to wifi by giving the wifi connection a static IP address. It's easy...
A. Settings | Wi-Fi
B. Click the info link next to the TP router name - you need to have already connected to it before
C. Under IP address, click the "Static" button
D. Give the connection a static address (I used 192.168.1.115 because that had been assigned to my phone by dhcp earlier)
E. Give the connection a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0
F. When you connect the iPhone to the TP, you'll see that it has no internet on the connection. You'll maintain your 3G/4G connection as well as the wifi connection to the TP. Setup Dropbox photo upload (or Amazon, iCloud, whatever) and every pic you take gets transferred. Just be careful of your data plan.

Hope the extra info helped. I'll come back and edit if I come across any other tips.

title: Disenchanted with Kindle ebook and (most) Kindle Customer Service Reps
text:
This single star reflects my disenchantment with Amazon's Kindle service representatives more than the Kindle itself, although I'm not happy with the Kindle ebook either. I give the Kindle a "2" star rating for the annoying way they changed the Kindle interface from "e-library" to "social media center".

Back in April 2017, the "Home" button on my beloved but elderly 4th Generation Kindle ebook (with special offers) stopped working (it's a physical button below the bottom of the screen, not an on-screen button.) The ebook worked perfectly in every other way, I could still use the ebook to read with, but it was annoying having to back out of everything using the back button instead of the Home button. At this point, I upgraded to a Kindle Paperwhite as I thought having a backlit screen would be useful.

I found I didn't like the Paperwhite because the interface you deal with to keep your documents in order is not set up the way the old ebook was set up, which is the way a computer filing system is set up.

On the old ebook, I had a couple of dozen "Collections" that I thought of as folders, and any book that hadn't been assigned to a Collection/folder would sit on the top directory, easy to see, right after the alphabetical list of Collection/folders.Once you assigned a document to a Collection/folder, it would handily disappear from the top directory and into the Collection, so all you saw were the books you hadn't assigned a Collection, plus new documents I imported or bought would pop up on the list. It was a great system as it meant minimal clutter on my interface and an easy way to find/navigate the 700+ documents I had there.. Just like in a "real" filing system on a real desk, or on a computer desktop: once you stick a document in a folder, it disappears into that folder, but it doesn't obscure the "current" documents that haven't been assigned to folder yet. Simple & easy!

Sadly, in the Paperwhite, if you assign a document to a Collection, you still see that document sitting on your top directory, it just gains the notation that it's now in a collection--which is useless! It becomes a real problem when you have more than 700 documents on your Kindle, as I do. I can assign all of them to Collections, but you'll still see them sitting on the top desktop, either floating around as bookcovers or in a long, long list on dozens of screens and in no useful order. Conversely, if I choose to see only Collections on my top interface, that is all I see: just the Collections/folders, and none of the books that haven't been assigned to Collections yet. I can't pick that as my go-to interface because the loose, unCollected books and new books that might pop in can't be seen in that mode.

This is like having 700+ documents on your desk with little sticky notes on each one saying what folder they should be stuck in. Maximum clutter! Or a couple of dozen folders full of documents sitting on top of the documents you need to deal with, but you can't get to them or even see them because of the folders sitting on top of them.

This is why I didn't choose and iPad back when I got my first Kindle. The iPad is designed for maximum clutter, with all your books floating around, begging for attention. I prefer my ebook to work more like a PC or laptop computer in its filing system, and I don't have that anymore with Kindle.

HERE IS WHERE THE KINDLE CUSTOMER SERVICE PROBLEMS START:

PART 1: APRIL SHENANIGANS: CLASSIC BAIT-AND-SWITCH

In April 2017, I called Kindle to complain about this change in the interface of the Kindle and ask if it was possible to get the old interface, figuring maybe I just wasn't hitting the right buttons, but the Kindle reps apparently didn't understand that the interface had changed from previous generations of Kindle ebook! I had to keep explaining over and over the way my old ebook had worked. The Kindle reps kept bouncing me around the system for about an hour.

Amazon Kindle reps who don't understand what your problem is or can't fix it for you default to bouncing you out to Amazon Retail with no explanation to anyone, which confuses Amazon Retail reps because they can't do anything with Kindle problems, so they bounce you right back over to Kindle. Each time it happens, you have to re-introduce yourself and re-explain the problem.

I finally got a Kindle service rep who told me that if I just replaced my old ebook with a new, simple ebook for $79, I'd get my old interface back. He literally told me flat-out that the Paperwhite had the new cluttered "social media center" interface, but not the current generation of ebook,which was simplified. The ebooks, he said, operated the old way. Also, he could get me a 20% discount on the new, simple ebook as I was replacing a broken ebook. THIS WAS ALL A FLAT-OUT LIE, LIE, LIE. That was April.

When I got the ebook in May, I found that it had the same annoyingly cluttered interface as the Paperwhite. (And I mean, seriously, if you like Goodreads, good for you, but I really don't care about the opinions of a bunch of people I don't know, so why can't I remove that annoying app from my interface?)

There was literally no reason whatsoever to buy the ebook, plus the 20% discount he told me would appear in my invoice hadn't happened, I had paid full price. I had been massively bait-and-switched by an Amazon Kindle customer representative!

PART 2: MAY KINDLE CUSTOMER SERVICE REP SHENANIGANS

I spoke to 3 Amazon representatives on May 4 and it took an hour and eighteen minutes to (partly) resolve my problem.

The first Kindle rep did the usual tactic where he realized the problem was complicated so he bounced me over to Amazon retail customer service. The Amazon retail rep had to apologize that he could do nothing to help with Kindle and that the first Kindle rep should not have done that (no, really?!), sending me back to Amazon Kindle (45 minutes and counting to get to this point) where I got Karoline R., a Kindle customer rep. Karoline had to struggle with the computer to fix this because the bait-and-switch Amazon Kindle rep I spoke to back in April had royally screwed up my Kindle account, so the computer fought her every step of the way. Karoline did her best to fix this, at least the part where I returned the ebook and got my money back, so she was a great Kindle rep, but every other Amazon Kindle rep I spoke to either tossed me back to Amazon Retail or screwed things up badly. She explained that the Kindle media interface is the same on all Kindles now, and there is no way to go back to the simpler "library reader" way of doing things.

Also: there is really no effective way to register a massive complaint like a lying bait-and-switch customer service rep.

Amazon needs to have more oversight on their Kindle reps because the names of the reps who screwed up (tossed me to someone else or bait-and-switched me) got away with it because their names aren't associated with their screw ups. Every time a rep speaks to someone, their name should automatically be associated with the action in both the customer's records and theirs. You as a customer shouldn't have to keep a list of the people you talked to, but I suggest you do, as I should have.

So, I was finally able to return the Kindle ebook with a maximum of effort, though I still have the Paperwhite and of course, nobody is able to help me fix my problem with the annoying interface. Why did they change the interface to become more clumsy and cluttered, more like an iPad? If I wanted an iPad, I'd have bought one. Why can't the Kindle work like a computer desktop works, the way it used to work?

I answer myself: the hard-working Kindle reader-as-convenient-library has become a slap-happy "social media center".

I have done a complete turn-around from adoring my Kindle to mildly detesting it. I will be investigating other ebooks at this point.

title: This camera takes really nice pictures when in full light and out of the ...
text:
I have had this sports action camera for a couple weeks now. It comes with a variety of clips, mounts, and tethers in addition to the waterproof housing and a remote (see the product description for a full list of accessories).

This camera takes really nice pictures when in full light and out of the waterproof case. Full resolution videos look great too. The camera does not have a built in flash, so low light pictures/videos are not good. Underwater pictures and pictures taken through the waterproof housing are not as clear, but comparable to other cameras of this type that I’ve used. I have fully immersed the camera in water while it is in the waterproof housing, and the camera stays completely dry.

I took pictures of roses in 12MP wide (4608 x 2592) and 4MP wide (2648 x 1504) for comparison. I put these pictures side-by-side to upload, but due to picture compression, it is difficult to analyze the results after uploading.

Before compression, the 12MP pictures could be digitally zoomed much more than the 4MP before pixelation. The wide angle fisheye lens took me a little bit to get used to, but it is nice to be able to get such a wide shot in one picture.

The menu is easy enough to figure out, using the mode button, shutter button, and side buttons to move through the options. One downfall is how the camera starts over on naming the photos each time they are removed from the camera (i.e., when I got to upload the pictures to my laptop, there are already pictures there named FHD0001, FHD0002, etc.). Other cameras that I own do not do that--they pick up where I left off even after the previous pictures have been deleted from the memory card or camera.

This camera has a playback feature that one of my other cameras does not. In summary, I like this camera, even though I really don’t see the need to set it up on my wifi network.

I purchased this camera at a discount in exchange for my honest review. I did not receive any other compensation, and I am not obligated to write a favorable review. I have used this product myself, and all words in this review are my own.

title: Great app for managing internet access and time limits.
text:
This product hits a good niche and so far seems to work well. My setup: I have a Netgear router. The features that it used for content filtering and limiting access were not very good and difficult to use and adjust. This app makes setting up usage limits, viewing usage and doing content filtering VERY simple and straight forward.

The good: after getting all the devices set up and profiles added for the family, it seems to work very well. I am able to see a break down of usage on the applications as well as internet activity. The time limit and bed time features work fine. Kids need to do chores? No problem... I can easily "pause" internet access.

Could be better: We have multiple devices that we use. Phones, Desktop computers, tablets, gaming consoles, Apple Tv, Smart TV's, etc. In some cases I had to go in and look at the devices mac address to identify it and assign correctly.

Some quarks: when using an iPad, if the kids aren't playing games that require wifi/internet access, it doesn't count towards their limit.

Cool features I didn't realize it had: my daughter ran out of her allotted usage and called me when I was at the grocery store. It was Father's day and she asked nicely so I was OK with her using a little more time. I was able to use the app over cellular to update her time limit so she had another hour.

If you are a parent and want to get a little more visibility into how much time your kids are spending on the Internet, and be able to easily manage and control their access, I think this is a great choice. I am looking forward to more features and future updates, but so far it has already met my expectations.

title: I really wanted to like these buds... Don't let the marketing fool you
text:
I will make this brief but to get right to the point: these are not good headphones.

They are lousy for a couple reasons.

1.) The sound quality is poor. (I am not an audiophile but can appreciate a good pair of headphones.) The mids are flat, the treble is exceptionally tinny, and... did they forget the bass? Even when I forced a seal by manually pressing the buds into my ear (see my complaint below) the sound was terribly weak.
2.) A lot of 5 star review rant and rave about the fit of the buds; despite giving all possible configurations a test, none worked for me. Jaybird provides you with 6 possible configurations for earbud fit,S,M,L in both silicon buds and the comply eartips; none of them worked for me. The foam tips never formed a seal in my ear and, as a result, the sound suffered and having earbuds fall out of your ear when pressing 300lbs is annoying. The silicon tips were also awkward, the biggest size would seal for about 5 seconds and then fall out. I have used many other silicon tips before without this issue.

It seems as though Jaybird has spent loads of money on marketing. I WANTED to love these buds but just could not make them work.

I hated these earphones, but gave them 2 stars because the Bluetooth connectivity was solid - i did not have one skip. Do not be fooled by the 5 star reviews - STAY AWAY.

title: Great travel lens!
text:
I'm preparing for an overseas vacation and I need to travel light. I was originally planning to bring my full-frame DSLR and three zooms (combined coverage of 16-200mm) but I quickly put that idea to rest due to the number of lenses and WEIGHT! So, I began my quest for the "perfect" travel lens which had to meet the following requirements (in order): Broad focal range, good image quality, small and lightweight, and reasonable price. Needless to say, I didn't have high hopes.

Ok, first, focal range. I wanted something with a broad range to replace two of my heavy lenses (Canon EF 24-70mm f/2.8L and Canon 70-200mm f/2.8L -- a combined weight of 5 pounds). It came down to this Tamron lens and Canon's EF 28-300mm f/3.5-5.6L IS USM Lens. Both the Canon and Tamron fit the bill in this category since 28-300mm should pretty much cover it all. Regarding image quality, being a "pixel peeper", I usually look at my shots at 100% in Lightroom on an iMac 5K (great computer/display, BTW). I read a lot of reviews that said the Tamron had surprisingly good (sharp) IQ, but the same was said about the Canon lens. I pored over MTF charts and sample images, both lenses seemed to have acceptable sharpness and contrast for the types of photos that I'd be taking while traveling. Next was size and weight. Canon's lens is big and heavy (3.7 pounds) and uses a push/pull zoom whereas the Tamron is lightweight (1.2 pounds) and uses a twist zoom. Clearly Tamron is the winner here. And lastly was price. The Canon lens is 3X the price of the Tamron. I already own expensive Canon "L" glass and don't want to spend a small fortune for a travel lens that gets used only a few times per year. Tamron is again the clear winner in this category.

So, I bought the Tamron. I mentally prepared myself for soft images and barrel distortion (especially the wide shots). After taking numerous photos over the weekend and viewing them in Lightroom (RAW images, 100% zoom on a 5K display), I can say that I am completely blown away by the Tamron lens. It's very sharp with good contrast, at times I thought I was looking at shots taken with my expensive "L" glass. The barrel distortion was very pronounced at the wide end (I knew this going in) but the folks at Adobe included a lens profile for Lightroom which completely mitigates the distortion (and vignetting). In addition to the phenomenal zoom range, the AF was quick and silent and the VC (image stabilization) worked very well. I am extremely happy with this lens and I'm looking forward to leaving it attached to my 5D Mark III for my upcoming trip (actually, I'll probably take the 6D due to it being slightly smaller/lighter).

So, in summary, I have fallen in love with the Tamron AFA010C700 lens (my first non-Canon lens). It essentially replaces two heavy lenses (at a whopping 5.1 pounds) with one smaller lens (1.2 pounds). No, It won't replace my "L" glass when I do professional work, but it will be firmly attached to my camera when I travel on vacation. The Tamron is small, lightweight, solidly built, with great IQ and features that work. I look forward to some fantastic vacation memories made with this lens.

Since these are worn around the neck, it's not like I'm abusing them. I use and charge them at least five days out of the week. I would not recommend this model based on them needing to be replaced every month.

Loss of sound aside, I still wouldn't recommend this model. They look great, which is why I wanted these over any other model of bluetooth headset, but they have the most uncomfortable earbuds that I've ever used and I've never had a problem with comfort with any pair of earbuds. Ever. The plastic part of it is short and fat and they don't fit in the ear correctly or comfortably and I often have to readjust them just to make them bearable.

I can't comment on actual audio quality since I'm not an audiophile and I just don't have the ear for something like that, but I think they sound just fine.
