title: Absolutely amazing laptop! But be sure that you know what you sacrifice for a great powerful machine
text:
This machine is astoundingly great! Right out of the box, the machines boots into installation and quickly sets you free to do what you want to do. Zero bloatware or unnecessary manufacturer applications can be found when you first boot to the desktop(save for the control center which is incredibly useful for monitoring thermals, fans, RBG, and performance). The keyboard is very tactile and a absolute pleasure to perform work on. The screen is as you expect if you used a 120htz display before. Wifi connection and Bluetooth is above average with very little or any instability. Overall thermal performance is above average as well! When you're doing moderate to light work, about 50-60 °C average for cpu. Gpu can be a mix as it really depends if your system is using it in your application, I get about 30 to 40 in my experience.

Now gaming and battery performance are ones that you should absolutely take note of. Gaming on this machine is incredibly nice with high performance in many games! However, this is important.... It will get toasty.. Toasty to where your hands can start to feel the burn. The outer metal shell will conduct the thermal heat as you might expect, causing the surface to be hot to the touch. It won't set your house on fire hot or cause the system to melt inside out. But if you plan to play games at high setting for any prolong period of time, be sure to keep this laptop well ventilated with either a stand or a stack of note card. Not a deal breaker for me since I expected this especially in a form factor like this.
The battery is where it really hurts, in overall casual use, not gaming, the battery can last up to 3 to 4 hours. If you're hopping between your classes or have a power outlet near you, its not really a problem. But! If you're at your local Starbucks, and you see a bunch of mac users hogging all available outlets, you'll start to appreciate laptops that last a long time if you ever owned one. Gaming on the otherhand demands you to be hooked up to the wall. Battery life plummets to the 1 to 2 hours depending on how power hungry the game you're playing is. Be sure to keep that I mind! Don't expect for this machine to last an entire day on a single charge!

With that in mind I highly recommend this machine to any gamer or student out there in a the market for a portable, great value, performance laptop right now. But beware the issues and keep them in mind when spending your cash.

title: Big sound...small footprint
text:
I just received this item a couple of hours ago and it has already impressed me. I keep glancing over to make sure that the very solid sound quality is emanating from that very compact speaker. When mine arrived it was partially charged. I completed that process in about 1/2 hour. The instructions that come with the unit are somewhat sparse. While charging a red led near the charging port glows. When charging is complete the led goes dark. Also, the instructions don't include the fact that a short press on the "-" button (volume down) will move to the next track, whereas a short press of the "+" button will move to the last track. Long presses on either such button will lower or increase the speaker's volume. You can also control volume through the connected device. This is similar to other Bluetooth 4.0 devices I've used. Also a short press on the telephone button will pause a track whereas a second press of that button will resume play.

I haven't used the phone feature yet, and frankly I'm not too concerned about it anyway since that's not why I bought this speaker. I'm no audiophile but I do appreciate a good sounding speaker. This one sounds much larger than it actually is. This speaker is about the size of the old transistor radios I used to have as a kid, but there is no comparison when it comes to sound. This is hands down far superior to other small speakers I've had before. There must be some serious engineering behind this product. Its appearance is sharp, and even though I checked its size and weight before ordering I was surprised to see how small and lightweight it is in one's hand.

I did crank it up to full volume, and of course the sound quality suffered. But even at 1/2 volume it puts out enough sound to fill a large bedroom. If you're looking to blow the doors off you probably aren't looking for this one anyway. But I'm betting anyone buying this will be pleasantly surprised by the sound it does produce. Very decent bass, good mid-range and highs.

This will easily fit into a pocket for travel. I haven't tested its water resistance, and I don't intend to do so. But I'm at least confident based upon its stated ratings that, if I accidentally drop it into water or leave it where it gets splashed or rained upon I should be safe. And it should survive a trip to the beach or pool, which is a use I very well may try.

Since I received this only a couple of hours ago I haven't tested the battery life. Supposedly it will play for up to 5 hours, and if it even gets reasonably close I'll be fine with it. I suppose the type of music and volume will influence battery life. If I find any significant deviation from the manufacturer's claims I'll update this review. I also haven't tested the bluetooth range, but again this isn't something about which I am terribly concerned. I have my phone about 5 - 10 feet from the speaker and it has been playing wonderfully with no dropped signal at all.

For the price I don't think you can go wrong with this one. You'll get a great bluetooth speaker for about half the cost of other comparably rated speakers.

title: Comprehensive review of this system - Conclusion: Best Bang for the Buck I have found!
text:
I am going to leave a very comprehensive review from my experience of owning this system for the past few weeks.
To start, I have been researching security camera systems for a couple of years now, since my neighborhood experienced a number of car break-ins. Last year, I bought a $700 Samsung security camera system that was decent quality. That system required that each camera be wired back to the DVR. A year passed, and that system has never been installed. I could not find an easy way to run wires from all corners of the house back to a single hub. It would have required an extensive amount of work, and the install quality would have been low.
So after a year with an uninstalled camera system, I decided to research wireless options. I knew that running just a power cord would allow me to very easily cameras anywhere around the house.
I researched for several weeks and read reviews for all of the wireless camera systems. I found that Xmarto had the best reviews and decided to get one of their systems. I chose the 4 camera system without a hard drive, and ordered the hard drive separately.
Installing the hard drive took literally 2 minutes, and you need no technological ability to do so - it is easy.

Installation of cameras:
Piece of Cake! The cameras are each mounted to the wall or eaves of your house using 3 screws. The wire runs out the back and is about 10” long before it connects into the power cord. The included power cord gives you about ten feet of range to find a plug. Three of my four cameras were within ten feet of a plug, so install was as simple as mounting the camera and plugging it in. One of my cameras ended up about 20 feet from a plug, so I ordered a cheap power cord extender, drilled a small hole in my garage wall, and plugged it in the garage.
Total install time of the 4 cameras was probably 1.5 hours, and was as easy as it gets.

Setup:
I had previously used IP cameras which were always impossible to set up and get working. This system is the exact opposite. I plugged in the NVR to power, and ran an HDMI cable between the NVR and my TV. Within 30 seconds of powering on, all camera feeds showed on my screen! It doesn’t get any easier than that!
The camera feeds show the signal strength in the corner of each image, so I went around and adjusted the antenna on the cameras to get the best signal. (My furthest camera is about 70 feet from the NVR, and through 2-3 walls).
By default, the system was set to record 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. I left it that way, and it should record for 30 days on a 1TB hard drive.
Lastly, I wanted to be able to view the cameras remotely on my phone. This is where I always had trouble on the old cameras I used to have, and I expected this to take some effort. Not the case! I downloaded the app, followed the easy instructions, and within 10 minutes, I had video on my phone! I went to the store to make sure it worked away from my house, and sure enough, I had remote video monitoring!
Total setup time from plugging in the NVR to having video on my phone was probably 20 minutes. This is incredible.

Quality of cameras:
The build quality is excellent, and actually better than the cameras from that very expensive Samsung system I own. These cameras are metal body, and solid. In CA, we just experienced a major rain and wind storm over the past 2 days. All cameras survived the storm with no issues!
Video quality is the best I have seen on a security camera system. During the day, you can make out license plates, small facial details, and vibrant colors. At night, the quality is surprisingly good. Of course, daytime quality is best, but you are still able to see great detail at night, and at a far distance. 960p HD is a lot of resolution. I can zoom into images quite a ways, which allows for better viewing of faces, etc.

Does it catch bad guys? YES! I bought this system for home monitoring, as well as security. Little did I know, that within a few weeks of install, it would catch a would-be car burglar in action! Last night, a man came onto my driveway and tried to break into my SUV. He left after seeing that there was nothing inside. I would never had known this occurred unless I had this camera system. I shared the images on my neighborhood website, and a neighbor responded that their car had been broken into. Because of my system, we now have a timeline of when the crime occurred, and a description of the system. Other neighbors have emailed me asking about my camera system, as they are very impressed with the quality. I think that I will have at least a few neighbors who will purchase this system to protect their properties.

Customer service:
Amazing! I emailed them to ask about the dreamliner software update, and they quickly provided detailed instructions on how to download it. They let me know that I should reach out to them if I need any assistance with the system, ever.

Overall impression:
After a lot of research and first hand experience, I believe this system is the best overall available right now, and at a great price! If you are researching systems like I was, stop now, order this, and you will be happy.

he machine I received looked like new but had a hard drive that went bad during my installation. This wasn't the seller's fault and probably worked fine when they tested it. What's really nice about these machines is you can upgrade and replace just about everything by sliding a metal plate off the bottom of the machine with no tools. There are some minor negatives, but not worth taking a star off for the price paid. The screen resolution is only 720P, but for a 14 inch display, its adequate with a crisp bright image.

This machine came loaded with Windows 10 but doesn't have a driver for the finger print scanner nor is there a driver available for the modem, but who uses those today anyway? The image that came with the hard drive had the HP drivers already installed, but because I had to do a fresh install of Windows 10, I had to find quite a few drivers on HP's site. (HP does not have Windows 10 native drivers, but the Windows 8.1 driver worked just fine)

Other than those minor niggles, this is an excellent machine for the money which rivals new machines costing many times more. I highly recommend this to anyone looking for a well built laptop.

title: Great for the bank fisherman, or checking banks where the boat can't go.
text:
I purchased the iBobber in July, 2014 and I am extremely happy with it. I don't own a boat and I do a lot of bank fishing. The iBobber helps me find fish when they are there, and perhaps more importantly tells me if there are NO fish where I am fishing. Then I know not to waste my time there. It is easy to cast and I have not had any issues with syncing the unit to my iPhone 5.

There have been some issues, and I have received a couple of replacement units as a result. The customer service is outstanding. Unless I email on the weekend, I always receive a response from Alex in well under 24 hours, usually the same day. They clearly want all of their customers to be happy.

I read all of the reviews on Amazon prior to mine, and I experienced some of the same issues described there. ReelSonar customer service addressed each of them, and replaced the unit if they felt necessary. They also offered to refund the price of the unit, even though I did not purchase it directly from them.

Regarding all of the comments about sync issues, I first thought the unit wasn't syncing until I read in the instructions "bluetooth ball continues to spin" , even though the display says "Connected". We are used to seeing the little ball go away, but in this case it doesn't mean the device is not connected.

This is not a boat mounted unit. If you reel it in to fast or drag it behind your boat so that it's thrashing about, splashing, and making bubbles, it won't give you good information. If you put a bubbler under a boat mounted sonar it would have the same problem. An earlier version appeared to have a problem with identifying some non-fish artifacts as fish, but that has been resolved. Battery life has also been improved, but don't expect to get the best battery life if you use the light and/or audible alarm. Of course, it also has the same limitations as any other sonar. For example, it cannot see fish at/near the surface.

It is unfortunate that many of those who wrote critical reviews did not give ReelSonar customer service an opportunity to address their issue. The company is clearly focused on making the product better and from my perspective they are using the customer feedback to make a better product.

The iBobber is an excellent product that does what it is designed to do very well.

title: Mildly disappointed.
text: I am mildly disappointed. I have an Amazon Fire Stick and a Roku 2 that we have been using on our televisions for over a year. We liked them both. No troubles with either of them. Recently however, the Fire Stick was starting to take 4-5 minutes to load. Once it did it ran great, but I decided not to chance a failure and replace it. We chose the Fire Tv over the Roku 3 because it has a feature(on pause it shows the actors names and other roles they have played) that my wife enjoys. Now, I will lead with the positive. The Fire Tv is a very easy install. The set up was easy and it picked up my network right away. The picture was great and the sound seemed better to us than the Fire Stick it replaced. We have not had any of the issues with the remote that others have reported. Works great.So far. Now for the negative. This is a big one for us because we need a wireless headset for my wife to use while I work at my computer. Our unit will not pair with Bluetooth headphones. The headset that I purchased was the Kinivo BTH240. I tried four times. Three times the Fire Tv recognized the headset, then it would not finish the pairing. Thinking it was the headset I paired it to my computer. Perfect. No trouble. Then, thinking it was a television issue, I tried it on the other tv. With the old Fire Stick. After a 5 minute warm up, the old Fire Stick was paired with the Kinivo headset in 30 seconds. Back to the Fire Tv. 5th try.It will not pair with this Bluetooth headset. I have since made a Sony radio frequency headset work with the Fire Tv using a Sabrent usb external stereo sound adapter, so we will keep this unit. But it does not function as advertised. If a Bluetooth headset is not important to you, you can add one star to my review. If I have any other issues with the Fire Tv, I will update this review and deduct stars accordingly. Thanks for taking the time to read my review.

title: Solid performer - recommended! One small note though.
text:
I must commend the Logitech M510 Wireless Mouse for being a solid-feeling and inexpensive device. The receiver is small enough to work with a laptop and be inconspicuous, and the easy-to-toggle power switch on the bottom makes turning it off to save batteries easy. The mouse feels a little heavier than a wired version with the batteries in - that takes a little getting used to and I had to tweak my windows mouse settings but no big deal there.

The two side-buttons (programmable, of course) - have a soft-push feel to them, not clicky, but are comfy to use. I get a lot of precision when using this mouse and would recommend it for anyone who is just sick of yet another cord in their computer setup. Me, I was tired of my cat laying on the cord when he sleeps between keyboard and monitor. Problem solved!

There are those who will tell you a wireless mouse is terrible for gaming, but I disagree. The real potential problem issue is a little more complex. For example, the third time I used this mouse, when operating it I heard strange scraping sounds from the front yard of my house. I opened the blinds and saw nothing at first, so I went back to using the mouse... heard it again. This time when I looked, I noticed some fir-tree rounds that had been sitting by the rubbish bins from a recent tree we had cut down had been dragged halfway across the lawn and left furrowed trails of moist brown upturned dirt behind. I reached down and gripped the M510 again and moved it left and forward, and watched the sections of wood drag a torn pathway through the rhododendrons growing along the edge of the lawn and then crunch into the side of my neighbor's Land Rover.

Needless to say there was a little bit of insurance paperwork to do, and I had to call in an Earth Wizard from the local council of elders to alter the frequencies of the magical force-lines around my property.

After that - smooth sailing! Can't recommend this mouse enough, but do be careful.

title: It works but is very temperamental
text:
When this arrived I was more than pleased! It was packaged very well and looked brand new! Plugging it in and setting it up was a breeze, and logging into all my streaming accounts like Netflix, Amazon Prime and Hulu was not difficult at all. Dvd and blu-rays played wonderfully and without any problem.

The problems started a short 1 month after it's arrival. Within about 4-5 weeks the machine started freaking out every time I turned it on. I would hit the power button and turn on for about 5 seconds and then shut itself off. I'd have to sit there anywhere from 5-10 minutes waiting for it to stay on. I've been dealing with this temperamental machine for about 7 months (I'm obviously too lazy to bother with returns) and finally discovered a trick. If I don't hit the power button but go straight to the eject button to put the disc in, the machine will turn itself on and actually STAY on.

Is if frustrating to deal with the fussiness of this machine? Yes, but I guess that's the trade off of buying a refurbished machine. It has definitely made me think twice about purchasing refurbished items in the future, and I wouldn't really feel comfortable recommending this Blu Ray Player to anyone else. I would say, buyer beware!

title: This was a tough review to write...
text:
This was a tough review to write as I really liked some aspects of the case, but almost hated certain other aspects of it.

Appearance: This case is stunning to look at - both front and back. I purchased the "Rose Gold" color to go with my rose gold iPad. If you look at the picture showing the back of the case, you'll notice that it complements it very well. There is also a circular cut-out at the back of the case which displays the Apple logo. It just adds more to the appearance of the case.

Design & Functionality: This case has two parts to it. (a) The "so called" leather part which opens and closes. The case stays closed with the help of a magnetic clasp. (b) Hard plastic attached to the back part of the leather. So basically, you flip the case open, and then snap the iPad onto the hard plastic.

Important - note that the entire back of the hard plastic is not affixed onto the leather part. Just half of it is. This is because the manufacturer wanted to add a swivel feather to their design. This way you have the ability to use this case to stand your iPad either horizontally, or vertically when viewing something on it. On the flip side, because the entire back of the hard plastic is not attached to the leather part, the iPad flips and flops a lot out of place. This can get quite frustrating!

There is a little elastic insert on the side of the case to hold your Apple Pen, which is a nice added feature. There is also an elastic handle that you can slide your fingers under when holding the case in your hand. However, that feature hasn't been that useful for me.

Protection: As long as your case is closed with the magnetic clasp in place, I think it will withstand a short fall. However, if it falls from your hand while you are using it (i.e. with it's top flipped back), you could cause some damage to the iPad. Reason being, as mentioned above - the entire back of the hard case is not attached to the leather part, hence not offering full stability.

Case Durability & Quality: I did read some reviewers complain about the stitching coming apart. However, I have been using this case regularly for a couple months now, and the stitching is still in tact. The leather part (which I do not think is leather) does seem to be durable and of good quality. However, the hard plastic inside it seems to be quite cheap.

Price: It's an eye catching case that offers both horizontal and vertical viewing options. But definitely not the most convenient to use, as it turns around too much (swivel feature). I therefore I feel like it is a bit over priced at $16.99.

Overall, if appearance matters more to you, then go for this case. It is one of the finest looking iPad cases I have seen. But if convenience and ease of use take priority, then this is definitely not the case for you.

title: Canon adapter works
text:
OK, this is for the Canon EF/EF-S mount to M4/3 adapter. This is very different from most of the M4/3 adapters in that it's got electronics onboard to convert M4/3 signals to Canon and the reverse. So the Canon lenses are autofocus(for a given value of that), the lens stabilization works(if wanted) and the aperture can be controlled from the body(most important). I've tried this on three different Olympus Pen bodies of various vintages and it does work. It's more expensive than the other adapters because of the conversion electronics, much more than just a metal tube with two different lens mounts attached. .Downside is that autofocus hunts, I can find a body setting where it doesn't do that, but it's just about as easy to turn off autofocus and use manual focus. I usually am in manual mode anyway. All exposure options work with the different bodies. I have both EF and EF-S lenses, it works the same with both. Haven't tried it with any third-party Canon-mount lenses, and not likely to. The two I have fill what gaps there were in my lens collection.

Build quality seems good, contacts seem to be gold plated, lens and body mounts seem to be well made and the body is metal. Only plastic seems to be the internal baffle/cover, that's not really exposed to wear. Lenses lock to the adapter solidly and the adapter is tight to the Pen bodies. I just used it for some macro work, it performed fine with auto M4/3 extension tubes. Comes with caps, too.

title: Quality product with a reasonable price tag.
text:
As a photography enthusiast, I knew that eventually I wanted to get into flash photography. I mainly shoot automotive vehicles, but plan to do a lot of portrait work. Having already purchased and used an umbrella, the next step for me was to try out a softbox. After determining what I wanted to spend and what I wanted to do for photos I settled on the SMDV Speedbox S50 for these reasons 1. The product got overall great reviews. 2. The price of the product was reasonable. 3. They seemed to have corrected the deficiencies from previous product reviews (mainly the fiberglass rods). 4. The product itself is aesthetically pleasing, id be lying if I said that the sharp look of the softbox didnt help influence my purchase, thats just me being honest.

I promptly ordered my product and received it within a couple of days. The item was neatly packaged in its box, and reading the paperwork inside showed that the box is supposed to contain the softbox, the bracket, rods, speedlight holder, and bag (which for some reason was missing from mine but Ill get into that later). I unpacked and assembled the product after reading the directions. Right away I could tell that the product was a great piece. The material for the softbox itself doesnt look, feel, or seem cheap at all, and the new revised version has steel rods instead of fiberglass ones which is a definite plus. I dont want to deal with the hassle of purchasing more rods and replacing them if I dont have to, its just not worth it to me. The mounting bracket on the backside of the softbox is made of thick plastic that easily accommodates the sizes of my flashes (430ex, 580ex, and 600ex), in the future I do plan to test it out with the AD200 pocket flashes, which I hear have large heads. The plastic material for the mount I could see being a drawback for some people, but at this price point I dont see it as an issue whatsoever.

The setup for the softbox was simple, and overall getting everything together was a piece of cake. For this box I have a variety of flashes that I will be using, but overall, I have been using my 430ex III speedlite, which works very well when paired with this softbox. My other flash used is a yongnuo 580ex II, which I also had zero problems with. I have to say my favorite part of using this softbox has to be how quickly it is to break down. Squeeze the two clips on each end of the mount and the softbox collapses for easy transportation and storage.

Overall, the S50 is a great piece to my collection. At its pricepoint I have no regrets with having purchased it. My experiences with softboxes are unfortunately limited since this is my first, so I cant really give feedback as to how it compares to other brands. I would however be willing to purchase more of them, and more than likely will be adding an Alpha version to my collection in the near future. A word of advice from me would be to inspect the contents of your package to make sure that everything advertised by the box/ad is inside of it (that goes for any package really). For some reason the carrying bag for the softbox was missing in mine. I promptly contacted Legio to see if it would be a big deal to just send a bag out to me. I was directed to repackage the product and send it back to them in order for me to receive get it, which I refused. It wasnt a big deal for me to have the bag, otherwise I wouldve. Regardless of the outcome, Legio was responsive in addressing my questions, I probably wouldnt have any issues with doing business with them again.

title: Well... it's a power supply. But Samuel L. Jackson would approve!
text:
Pros:
- It's a power supply
- It works

Cons:
- It's a power supply
- It didn't come with a bevy of hot girls

Other Thoughts:
In my lifetime, I've reviewed a lot of tech products. And for some of them you might discuss the performance metrics, the compatibility issues, or even how much LED bling is plastered all over it -- because, as everybody knows, the PC market desperately needed to turn into a close facsimile of the car enthusiast community. Next, these folks will put chrome tips on their exhaust ports, and some enterprising wannabe Jedi will come along to to deliver a proton torpedo straight up the...

...Well, you get the idea.

So what can I say about this power supply? The Corsair RMX850X works properly. It has modular cables, which are black, and that's good, because we all know what system building was like during the days of IDE cables and power supply rat nests. What idiot thought up sticking random useless cables on every power supply they sold, anyway? And why did they have to come in multicolor, like Picasso smoking weed and throwing up all over the canvas? "What's that a painting of, O master of incomprehensible art?" "Why, my young apprentice, some time in the distant future, engineers will make ratty looking contraptions called 'power supplies' that will look something like multicolored wire vomit." "DMaster... can I have some of that [expletive deleted] weed you've been smoking?"

But hey, you buy this power supply, and you don't have to deal with it. The wiring is so black, it's speaking Samuel L. Jackson to me. "I'm tired of these [expletive deleted] snakes on this [expletive deleted] plane!" That's right, you buy yourself an RMX850X, and your PSU is Samuel L. Jackson.

Now, let me tell you what you get when you open the box. This power supply is so Samuel L. Jackson, it comes with fancy black bag with drawstring surrounding it. So you've got a perfect place to store your bling, and your cash if you ever take a job doing whatever Samuel L. Jackson was doing in Pulp Fiction. Not every power supply comes in a velvet bag, you know. And then you get some cables, which are nice if you actually plan to build a computer with it.

The voltages looked good. But unless you're buying bargain basement stuff that even the Chinese outsource because it costs too much to make, you'll get decent voltages. So that's kind of expected these days. I guess there's no real cons with the RMX850X, except that when you buy a Samuel L. Jackson power supply that comes in a velvet bag, inside a box *that* big, you kind of expect more. Like, if you opened that bag and a bevy of hot girls modeled your brand new PSU, delivered on a silver platter, with angels singing Pulp Fiction in the background like "Blessed is he, who in the name of charity and good will, shepherds the weak through the valley of darkness, for he is truly his brother's keeper and the finder of lost children. title: Hardware OK - Software and Documentation needs much improvement.
text:
Rating is a 3 because the hardware does what you would expect. The software is not even adequate.
I install security system cameras to capture the action around my home. It is important that the system accurately captures the action. It is perhaps more important that I can play back the captured video. That I can quickly and easily isolate the time and portions of the video that I have an interest in. Then to capture it. This is where this DVD is severely lacking.
It is hard to review this product because the Amazon review guidelines do not want you to use product names or use URL’s. The problem I have is that this product purports to support operating system devices that run Windows, IOS , and Android. Primarily using peer to peer (P2P) via Free APP XMEYE. Some devices do not work at all. Some have limited abilities and some work quite well. But XMEYE is not very good at any of the basic requirements of configuration, capture and playback. In fact it is a weak link in making this a fairly good product. The weakest link is the use of ActiveX as a browser addin on windows products.
The device was shipped without any documentation of any kind and no CD or anything. Not even a shipping list. Questions ask and answered on Amazon about this product point to a website where you can download the JZTEK DVR User Manual in pdf format. This manual is barely adequate. Does not cover anything in detail and is sorely lacking in how to make things work. It is going to require much trial and error in setting up this device for doing anything other than just letting it record and playback 24/7. This user manual needs major work in the area of encode setup, channel type, and alarm setup, just to configure basic function. It desperately needs to reviewed and rewritten to get rid of the Chinesenglish.
The only way you can setup this dvr with the best results is to add a display and mouse to the device. For the most part this works pretty well. I attached a 10" display via the HDMI port and a wireless mouse. The first problem with this is the default display resolution is set to 1280x1024. So my display would not work. They should set the default resolution to 1024/768. I believe all current displays will display this resolution.
The software does a pretty fair job of scanning and setting up the cameras. Once you have configured the DVR you will find that things just do not work. Like for instance if you set the time and date format to normal USA formats you will find that some things especially in playback do not display correctly. Like the date and time. Word spacing and formatting will be wrong. I need to clarify that it makes a difference as to whether you are accessing the DVR natively using the local mouse and monitor or whether you are using a browser pointed to the DVRs URL (ie. http:// YourDVRIPaddress:80) . I do not understand why.
The first things in the User manual is how to setup and use XMEYE. For instance it says
"Enter http://xmeye.net into the internet explorer ......". This is important because no windows software will access this device, other than the DVR native software using an attached monitor, except a browser with an ActiveX addin. Internet Explorer (IE) directly supports ActiveX once you have set the IE settings correct (Unsigned ActiveX for instance) this can be made to work. If you are running Windows 10, IE is not even installed on your system by default. You will have to add it. Windows 10 also sets security settings like User Account Control and Windows Smartscreen that will give you headaches in making this work. With older versions of Firefox and Chrome I have made ActiveX to work for these browsers. I have yet to get then to work with this ActiveX addin. The users manual needs to explain how to setup and install the activex addin for IE 11 on a windows 10 system
My experience with XMEYE is not good. Many things, especially related to configuration of the DVR do not work right. They often do not take. You will try over and over to get the device configured correctly. But you will not achieve it.
With ActiveX properly installed you can enter the http:// YourDVRIPaddress:80 to access this device. From here you can change configuration settings and view and play back the cameras. This only works to a degree. For some reason settings configured this way often do not take. One major problem is trying to set the motion detection region. I never could get this defined using browser access. It also does not work using XMEYE.
Because this software only runs on PC windows systems using ActiveX, if you have a system with a high resolution 4K screen you will not be able to see anything correctly. ActiveX apps do not follow Microsofts guidelines for High Resoliution displays. It expects the display scaling to be set to 100 percent. As this is not possible on your high resolution display which is often set to a scalling of 300 percent and resolution of like 3840x2160. I have multiple windows systems. The newest has a high resolution display. No matter what I did I could not get things setup so that I could read the screen
You cannot use the new Windows 10 Edge browser or most Smart TVs. They do not support ActiveX.
You can use IE to access XMEYE. XMEYE supposedly will run on Android and IOS devices by downloading an app. I have 3 android devices that I tested. XMEYE would not install on my IOS device. It would not install on my Amazon Android Tablet. It installed okay on two of my Android telephones but would crash on one of them. XMEYE did install OK on two phones by scanning the OR code from the phones.
This DVR supports AHD, TVI and CVI. You can mix and match camera types to a degree, It will support an IP camera but that will change the configuration of what cameras are supported.
Sometimes the playback functions of this DVR just quit working correctly. You try and play back a timed section and the DVR will not accept the action. The only way to fix it that I have found is to reboot he DVR. Sometimes XMEYE can not access the DVR. I have to reboot the DVR.
I can not recommend the purchase of this device, however there is not a whole lot of options available for DVR's that support a hybrid set of cameras. This could become a very good DVR with improvements in the software and users manual.

title: Great device for parents!!
text: The Circle device is like a dream come true for parents who have wanted to bring some balance and control to their family's use of the internet.  It is very simple to use, takes only a couple of minutes to set up, and allows you to monitor and set boundaries on the use of your home internet wi-fi network.  I love the many features, which include setting a "bed-time" for each person or each device.  My daughter, who is 16, was very resistant at first, but now she accepts a reasonable bedtime during the week, and asks permission for an "extension" on certain nights, such as weekends.  Without this boundary, she would be up into the very late hours every night, and not get the rest she needs to face school the next day.  I also like the ability to filter the content to protect my kids from inappropriate sites.  Circle allows you to set a different filter level for each user and/or each device, and also allows you to custom tailor the filtering to block specific sites or to allow specific sites.  It even allows you to adjust the settings remotely, when you are not even connected to your home network, as long as you are connected to the internet.  I especially like the ability to temporarily "pause" everything in the whole house (like at mealtime, for example), at the push of a simple pause button.  Circle is a very powerful and sophisticated device, but through it all, it is very intuitive and easy to use.  A great buy for any parent -- thank you, Circle and Disney!!

title: Very good performer at a very fair price.
text:
Although I slightly prefer the more expensive Moultrie S-50i I also just tested, this is a very competent game camera, and definitely better than the Bushnell Trophy Cam HD Essential E2 12MP Trail Camera I first bought in February.

Compared to the S-50i, this camera is significantly lighter and thinner left to right, with slightly lower resolution (16MP rather than 20MP, and uses 8 AAs rather than 12AAs.) It also settles for a 2 line monochrome LCD display rather than a full color multi-line display.

Compared to the Bushnell, its resolution is MUCH better, as the actual optical resolution of the Bushnell is only 3MP. This camera also costs a bit more, but the added cost is well worth it in my opinion, as is the further added cost of the S-50i over this model's cost, in my opinion.

All three have a fast 0.3 second trigger speed, and very satisfactory invisible infrared flash at night.

Actually, all three cameras are good enough to be useful, and I do in fact have all three in use, one watching my community garden plot, and the other two watching entries to our home and fenced yard.

My neighbor just borrowed this camera to see what was eating the oranges in his back yard, which turned out to be rats. He has rat bait stations, and this camera caught several visits to the bait station during the course of a night, leaving him to suspect the station is not doing its job.

Both my neighbor and I found the [[ASIN:B00P8A56PQ ARKON Heavy Duty Camera Clamp Mount with 1/4 20 Mounting Bolt for Nikon Sony Canon Olympus Panasonic Cameras]] much better for mounting the Moultrie cameras to boards around our homes than the supplied nylon straps meant to go around trees neither of us have in the proper locations.

Here are sample photos, showing how this camera sees our yard in daytime and at night.

Overall, entirely good enough for most needs, though I slightly prefer the S-50i.

Update 4/27/17: I was impressed that the camera got a good photo of a mourning dove flying across its field of view. It also got 2 good photos of the neighborhood maintenance staff checking the wood under our eaves last week.

title: Improvements have been made!!!!
text:
The box, it self, works great. It was an easy set-up and played right out of the box. I recorded a movie on it with no problems but when I looked at the flash drive I saw that it had taken a single movie and turned into 5 or 6 mp4 files. The downloaded software that comes from company also easily loaded. It was my belief that when burning a DVD the software would seamlessly merge the mp4 files and then convert them to standard DVD files typical of what you get when you purchase a DVD movie. Unfortunately this is where the problems started. Sometimes the software would convert the files but they would not be merged together. You would get about 20 minutes of a high quality video that would suddenly stop right where the first mp4 file had stopped. Using your forward or fast forward you could coax the DVD player to start playing the second mp4 file but would also stop at the end of that file. And so on. So, if you wanted to watch your movie you had to watch it in 4 or 5 intervals. Alternately on occasion the software would create a DVD but when I tried to play it on a Sony DVD player I would get this message: Cannot play this disk. I tried it on a Panasonic player and got the same result.
To their credit the people who are trying to sell the Cloner Box tried to help. We must have exchanged over 30 emails. I was constantly sending them the LOG file from the software. However, nothing they suggested worked. In fact, most of what they suggested I had already tried. So, I am not sure they really have a grasp of their product and expecially of their software. After I had ruined about 25 DVD disks I decided to send the box back to the tune of $16.75 (After all, it is not cheap to send something to China). In the email they sent me they said they would cover return shipping. Time will tell. If the refund does not come through at least I have Amazon to complain to and at that time I will update this review. Hope this helps!
One last thing, I really had high hopes for this product. It looked like exactly what I was looking for. Rather than being forced to use componet cables all you used were an HDMI cable. <sigh>
The refund for the return came back in a timely manner. Both the cost of the Cloner Box and shipping charges were refunded to my account. In addition to the refund I received a message from the person I had worked with to try to solve the problems mentioned above. She stated that the company has come up with a firmware update for the Cloner Box that will solve the problems mentioned earlier. Here is a part of the message she sent me: For the playback problem you mentioned, we have uploaded a new firmware. The new firmawre makes one file into NTFS USB drive directly now, and it won't stop during playback any more. HDMI-Cloner Box Firmware:
http://www.cloner-alliance.com/download.html
This suggests I should up the number of stars I have given this product but as I have not tried the improved Cloner Box I am reluctant to do so. I have tried another option, a PVR2, but it is giving me more problems than the Cloner Box. The PVR2 seems to be designed primarily for video games rather than videos in general. I suspect I will be returning the PVR2 and probably giving Cloner Box a second try. I will keep you updated if I do so.
I had hoped to write a new review but Amazon doesn't permit that. So, here is an update to the review above. This review is dated 6/29/15.
I tried a different PVR but had all kinds of problems with it. As I had received an email from Cloner Alliance saying they had fixed the previous problems I had experienced I decided to reorder HDMI-Cloner Box. I also downloaded their new version of Cloner Helper. Once again it was an easy set up. I also reformated my flash drive from FAT32 to NTFS (Very Important). I gave the box its first trial making a copy of one of my DVD's. The Box worked flawlessly. Instead of breaking the movie into 4 or 5 mp4 files it produced only one file which eliminated the need to merge files. The newer Cloner Helper took the one file and created a DVD that was a perfect copy of the one I played. I tried several other copies and the device worked great. The bottom line is that I am very pleased and now recommend Cloner Box

title: *This review is for the one with 3 USB 3.0 Ports* Highly Recommended
text:
I would definitely recommend this. I am using it with my desktop setup with MacBook Air. Mine sits toward the right of my monitor beneath. It is of VERY good build quality and the aluminum matches a MacBook/ iMac VERY closely. Also, the round sides as seen in pics resembles the sides of the Apple Wireless Keyboard/ Magic Keyboard. I am shocked that this is not from Apple themselves. This hub uses a USB 3.0 cable, you know, the kind that the Samsung Galaxy S5 used, as well as most USB 3.0 external hard drives. The cable included is very thick, but is only about 2 feet. Also, there is a power port on the back, which I assume is used to give more juice to the USB ports so you can charge a phone or power something such as a USB fan. This cable is not included , although I feel it should be at $20. I would even pay $25 to have the cable included, but it is $9.99 to buy it. I will most likely shop for one on Amazon or Ebay with identical power and cable type and get one a few bucks cheaper.

Ports
This hub has 3 USB 3.0 ports, and they are blue on the inside, unlike Apple USB 3.0 ports. To the left of these ports is a Micro SD card reader and to the left of that in the same section is a full sized SD card reader. This is espicially nice for someone like me who has an 11 Inch MacBook Air and does not have this.

The hub has a grey rubberized bottom which aids it to stay still when you are plugging and unplugging things. This is a nice touch.

TLDR:
Very nice quality, has spot for optional power cord to provide more juice to the USB Ports and it is not included, high quality USB 3.0 Cable included, looks very nice and matches MacBooks and Mac desktops, has grippy bottom, would look nice on almost any setup, has SD and Micro SD card slot, looks very nice. title: if you do understand how to setup enterprise routers then you will be happy with this model
text:
WARNING: I will repeat what other have said. This is not a "home" router that you would buy from a local retail store. The 3 ports do not come pre-configured for use out of the box. If you do not have knowledge of what a WAN, LAN, DHCP or DNS are then you need to skip this appliance. However, if you do understand how to setup enterprise routers then you will be happy with this model.

I purchased this appliance to replace my Untangle PC firewall. I used a PC as my "router" because I have a 200 Mbps Internet connection. Most routers would not give me my full bandwidth. Untangle running on a old PC with dual gigabit cards gave me about 190 Mbps. The EdgeRouter came with a firmware version of 1.2.0. This version of firmware is very old. Make sure to update the firmware to at least 1.9.0 before you begin the setup. The older firmware versions do not have all of the features that you will want.

NOTE: You cannot upgrade firmware version 1.2.0 directly to version 1.9.0. The upgrade will fail. You have to upgrade incrementally. I downloaded and ran each version update until I got the 1.9.0 installed. Once I had the latest firmware loaded I performed a factory reset. After a reset you will have the first time setup wizard run when you login. This makes the setup MUCH easier.

My EdgeRouter has been running for a few days now with no problems. My download speed is actually at 215 Mbps now. So this router squeezed out a few extra Mbps from my service. Yes, I know that the ISP limits the bandwidth. But I did get a performance boost from what I already had. Very happy with my purchase. (so far)

One final warning. This router has vent holes on the sides and top for a reason. They didn't put fans on it so make sure not to cover this device up or confine it to a small space. I am sure it would overheat quickly if not properly located or ventilated.

title: Not as good as other reviewers have claimed
text:
I have had a pair of the lg tone+ (hbs-730) for years but the power button broke and time to look for a new pair. I don't have a samsung phone so i couldn't compare the UHQ claims so this review is based on the standard connection you would get with any other phone.

My lg tones, in my opinion, sounded great with even sound and good bass and sounded like wired headphones and they served me well for years. The Samsung Level U Pro's came close to the sound that i am used to. The vocals or higher tones were great and clear and the bass was present but wasn't super strong or overpowering, personally a little more would have been welcomed. The mids on the other hand you can tell were missing. Listening to music you can tell something is missing and its a shame for such a nice set of headphones and the price you pay for them. Calls were clear and i was heard well, didn't get complaints from the calls that i did make and i am a quiet speaker so good on Samsung for that.

The earbuds hang in front and have magnets that hold them together. Its a nice feature and i never really got to use the answer/ hangup when you pull them apart. I work in an office and don't make calls much, very rarely. Over my use the dangling became an annoyance and i prefer buds that connect to the base. If you can get a good seal they sound good but the shape of them made it difficult to get them deep enough in my ear to get a good seal and they always felt a little loose.

Another thing that cause concern for me was the charging. Most of my headsets, once charged, stop the charging process and either turn off or a light stays on but the Level U Pro's seem to keep charging and when i got to work the next morning the battery area would be really warm. Warmer than should be for a headset, non others have ever heated up so i worry about how long this battery may last before failure. It was almost to a cell phone over heating temperature.

Overall, not too bad a pair, would mostly use them in an office, walking around but not running or anything that could cause these to bounce on the neck. Other headsets would be better for sports like activity. If the sound were better, fit better in the ears and the battery lasted longer than 8 hrs ( i work 12+ hr shifts) and didn't overheat when charging, i probably would've kept them but there are better products out there.

title: Small, responsive & versatile
text:
This Gana 3-Port HDMI Switch works well for us. It seamlessly turns one HDMI port into three and the remote control feature allows for easy tuning, especially if using a universal remote like a Harmony 650 (more on that later). This item has a very small footprint, which allowed me to mount it to the back of my TV. I used [[ASIN:B0184L8PVM 12 of VHB 3M Adhesive Double-sided Foam Tape High Bond Conformable Acrylic Glue Replacement Kit 1.5 x 3 Inch Rectangular Plus Alcohol Pad]] to accomplish the mounting, but this diminutive switch can surely be affixed by any number of methods.

There are several brands out there that look nearly identical and work exactly the same. In fact, I purchased this switch to replace another one that looks and functions the same, but that failed after 4-1/2 years. I first tried another brand (that also looks the same), [[ASIN:B071YF38KW SMARTOOO 3 in 1 out HDMI 1.4v switch 3 ports HDMI switch 4K / 3D auto switch / remote control]], but it did not smoothly switch from input to input and had to be returned. On the other hand, this Gana Switch is very responsive and works better than my original switch ever did and certainly better than the one I had to return. I also like that the indicator light on this unit is red, rather than obnoxiously bright blue.

This brand/model comes with a power cord, but it is not needed for my application as power is supplied by the devices installed as inputs (in my case a Roku 3). This switch works as described - I find I need the remote control feature because the auto-switch function is not as useful when you have inputs that don't power off (e.g. a Roku). I don't detect any difference in picture quality going through this device (I do not have a 4K TV or signal, so I cannot comment as to that).

While I need the remote control feature, I don't use the remote that came with the switch. Instead, I rely on a universal remote (otherwise I would need 5 remotes for the setup pictured). My remote of choice is this entry-level Harmony: [[ASIN:B004OVECU0 Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver)]]. There are more expensive Harmony remotes out there, but for line-of-sight applications this is all you need! This switch is compatible with the Harmony 650 remote, but it is not recognized by the MyHarmony App that programs the remote (this is the first device I've found that is not in Harmony's database). This means that the switch needs to be added manually, but there's a slight hiccup. When you follow the MyHarmony on-screen prompts it displays an error message about the model number being for a remote (not a switch), so you can never progress to the options that allow adding a device manually. The Harmony help forum & Google were of no help and I almost returned the switch. However, I realized since the switch was not recognized as a device in the Harmony database all I needed to do was enter a bogus model number (one that would not be mistaken for a remote control). Once I entered the bogus number, the on-screen instructions walked me through adding the switch manually. It has been working perfectly since then.

Summary:
Pros: Small, responsive, remote controlled, sensitive remote, red (vs blue) indicating light, 3 HDMI Ports from one.
Cons: Not in the Harmony device database, so harder to add to universal remote (but this is really a Con for Harmony, not Gana).
I recommend this product. The four-star rating will be upgraded depending on durability ( I want better than a 4-1/2 year service life for a higher rating).

title: KENSINGTON'S RARA AVIS:  A bag that delivers EXACTLY what is advertised AND MORE on Amazon!!!!
text:
In an era where little is ever delivered exactly as it is described, this Kensington 17" lockable backpack is a rarity. Although nothing is perfect - and I would like a brighter color interior to see items down in the deep/abundant pockets better, and few small changes made - overall the design, materials, workmanship, and functionality for a Million Mile intl business flyer like myself are as close to perfect for my needs as I have found. (photos to come)
I rarely if ever check a bag, because as all road warriors know, that is death to getting in and out of airports quickly or worse they get lost or tossed.
So having this spacious - yet easily stowed under most airplane seats/overhead bins - overnight bag is so helpful.
If you pack smart and it isn't dead of winter at your destination? One can easily pack two day's of business casual attire in the clothing section, plus a 15 inch MacBook Pro (in well padded area), 10.5 iPad + keyboard (also padded), headphones in case, digital camera, 10k backup battery/chargers + cables, two iPhones, sunglasses, readers, a Kindle, 750ml SIGG waterbottle (inside or in zippered exterior holder), keys (on provided clip), mini umbrella, magazines (if you still do that tree wasting stuff) and work folders with plenty of room to spare. Fully loaded, it rests as well on my shoulders as it does sitting atop my rolling carryon.
I don't need to reiterate the excellent descriptions and photos in Kensington's advert above only to say that all claims are true, and point out some important details that I don't remember them emphasizing:
1. This bag empty is VERY light for its dimensions: a huge plus in this era now that airlines weigh everything going on the plane (and no doubt soon will start weighing customers!)
2. The twill nylon exterior looks quite nice and seems good for resisting marks and tears (will update after a month on the road)
3. Unmentioned, the bottom of the bag has a high density, likely waterproof, rubberized PVC layer to protect against it being ruined on rough floors or in wet places.
4. There is a discrete yet handy top zip pocket just below the carry handle that accepts my RayBans in a hard case, or could take a passport + wallet, keys, and or a smartphone or two for easy access in airports etc.
5. As all laptop bags should, it has the lie-flat TSA friendly laptop section for those who aren't TSA Pre/Global Entry (in the USA).
6. The locking/tether system is the best I've seen, the zippers strong and solid, zipper pulls are a very durable metal. There is no way to get into this bag without destroying it - which makes insurance claims much more likely to succeed - should a dummy thief not just go past your bag to an easier one next to it.
In summary: This bag is well made, good looking, has all the features I need and is incredibly good Value For Money at about $95 delivered.
The ability to secure this bag in hotels without safes, open workspaces and airports/lounges/trains where you don't wish to constantly keep an eye on your bag while working, or drag it to the bathroom with you for a wee minute or two, is just invaluable to me on the road. If you carry around today's full business kit, you likely have some $3000-5000 of easily stolen/sold items in your bag -never mind your papers and passport. To be able to secure it all in a handsome $100 bag is IMO both a large dose of design magic and a no-brainer:
BUY THIS BAG.

title: The stiff neckline allows for good line of sight with baby. It is very cute looking and has pockets for rags.
text:
I think a good nursing cover is absolutely essential to new moms. Nursing is one of the hardest aspects of parenting for the first year. The first 3 months of my sons life I felt like that’s all I did! A good nursing cover allows mom to go out in public places and maintain her privacy, or even just have friends over and be able to sit in your comfy chair and feed your baby. I’ve used about 6 nursing covers and this is one of the better ones, although I have a small issue with it. Here are my brief thoughts:

• Neckline: This is the most important feature of nursing covers in my opinion. I HAD to be able to see my son nurse, so I needed one with a stiff neckline that kept the material pushed up so I could see my baby. My son is 18 months and we nurse once a day now, but in those first few months I often needed both hands AND needed to be able to see him for good positioning. When I had a nursing cover without the rigid neckline I got so frustrated! This Jasmine nursing cover has a wonderful, stiff (but bendable) neckline so the baby is always in view.
• Strap and rings: This is the only thing I would change about this cover. I dislike having the dual rings I have to thread the end of the strap through. Occasionally I’ve had problems with them coming undone or slowly loosening on my other covers. My favorite nursing cover has a purse strap type of set up around the neck. It can be tightened or loosened, but there’s no free end that you need to thread through the rings. Is this a deal breaker? No… But it is an area for improvement. I do have to say the “O” rings feel much more secure than the “D” rings on other ones.
• Design: This is the cutest design of nursing cover I think I’ve seen. I love the neutral gray and the subtle white nature designs. Very trendy and nice, especially for moms planning to have a few children as this is could work with either gender.
• Pockets: This is the only nursing cover I’ve seen with the pockets. I love them! These are perfect for a small washrag/burp cloth. I would always get done nursing and go to burp my son only to realize I left the burp rag somewhere else. I love how deep these pockets are. They also work as to add a tiny bit of extra weight at the bottom, which is nice in the windy weather.

Overall, I highly recommend this. The strap issue is pretty small, I would definitely rather go with this with the small strap issue, but that has pockets at the bottom, over another one. I’ve safety pinned my straps in the past that were slowly coming undone, or they could even be sewed. Whatever you buy, I encourage you to make sure you get one where you have line of sight of the baby. It’s so helpful! I have a 10 and 1 ½ year old. My older daughter I only nursed for 3 months, partially because I had to duck into bathrooms or spare rooms to nurse her and I felt socially isolated. She also had a hard time nursing and we never got it down. I was more determined with my son and although we had a rough start it’s actually gone well for us. I am a nurse and have a long term goal of becoming a lactation consultant to help other moms who have problems as well. I would say a good nursing cover, comfy chair, large water bottle, well padded nursing pillow and good TV series to watch on Netflix are all great things to have when you get started. I was sent this for review purposes, that has no bearing on my rating or review of it, this is my honest opinion.

title: Great Service, Not so great hardware.
text:
This review is for the Amazon Fire TV HARDWARE, not the service. To be clear, I love the Amazon Video service. The hardware, not so much. I have 3 of the Fire TV boxes, and 1 Fire TV stick. 2 of the Fire TV boxes and the Fire TV stick work pretty well, with only an occasional reboot needed...maybe every couple of months. It frequently will start up and say it has "Lost Network Connection", even though it is hardwired to the router, and everything else in the house, either hardwired or wifi, will be working normally. title: Frustrating Product
text:
This sounds great when it works. Issue is it does not work consistently due to the software required to use the product. You must use either the Sonos App (phone) or Sonos Controller (PC) to play music. These apps have to locate the "system" (the speaker(s) on your Wi-Fi network & these apps CONSISTENTLY cannot find the speakers. The app will then ask you to actually hard-wire the speaker(s) to the router!! (laughable) or perhaps re-boot the router (laughable). Like most families, I have a household of Wi-Fi devices; computers, ipods, ipads, android phones, Apple phones, TV's, PS4, XBOX, and all them work flawlessly with my network. I never have issues with any of them....except the SONOS PLAY ONE. This company does not know how to integrate the hardware & the software and it seems to be a work in progress. I would stay away and if you do not believe me, look at all the low reviews that all state the same issues.

Update: I am now giving this 2 stars as opposed to one. For some reason the controller has been better at finding the speakers. Maybe there was a software update. But is it still not what I consider reliable. However, it will eventually find the speakers after a few mins. So I have learned to just ignore the "Sonos cannot locate your system" error and simply wait 3-4 mins. The app will find the speakers eventually. This is not acceptable but hoping Sonos can provide an update to fix this really bad bug. When this is working, I really like it over other speakers. Sonos can find and play your entire music library including iTunes and any music files on your phone or PC. Plus it has a nice search function on the phone app for Amazon Music. The Echo app cannot search Amazon music (I find that amazing but true) but Sonos as a great search function. So, I am truly hoping these "cannot locate your system" errors go away with updates. With all the negative reviews, the company must know about the issues and would hopefully address them. Will report back in a few weeks.

UPDATE 2: Once again, the SONOS software is certainly a work in progress and not user friendly. SONOS just put out a major upgrade to the app & controller (v8.3). When I updated the controller, it did not complete & had errors. I tried again but message stated that the updated software already installed. Then I went to android SONOS app and updated. This worked without errors. However, when I tried to use the SONOS app on phone, it could not find my system. The controller on my PC found the system but only one speaker as I have 2 speakers. Basically I had to reset the entire system several times before it all worked again. I am in the IT industry and pretty "tech savvy" so I can just imagine a user who is not tech savvy trying to accomplish this upgrade. I LOVE the speakers when they work. They sound great. But the software needed to run the speakers is very iffy at best. I have 5 Amazon Echo's, 3 iphones, 2 Android phones, laptops, PC's, ipads, ipods, you name it. These all work seamlessly with my Wi-Fi and I never have issues with any of them. SONOS software does not always work seamlessly with the WI-FI and can be very frustrating. I would return it all but I can usually get it to work and I love the music when it works. But you better be tech savvy to manage the connectivity issues wit the software.

title: Problems if you're the kind of user who shortcuts a lot.
text:
So dang close.... but just not three.

This beast of a keyboard is a tour de force of creative, intentional redesign. I picked this up because despite being a big person I often feel my fingers are too Trumpy for for completely fluent typing.

It's astonishing that so much thought could be put into something and still to make unforced errors. I'm not talking about design decisions I kinda disagree with, but things I think are really quite unarguable.

The key wells are really really cool. They just work. The thumb button clusters are also really clever and work nicely.

My main complaint is that they unnecessarily moved the control and alt keys, and moved them in a way that makes it difficult to shortcut around. I have every possible combination of shifts, alts, ctrls and keys bound for quicker coding, and this screws all that up.

The control and alt keys— especially the alt key, which is only on one side— are hard to get at without re-positioning the hands. Do you alt+tab around different windows? Or crtl+tab and ctrl+shift+tab around your browsers? Well forget it. Reaching those— especially the 3-key-combos, is as unnatural as hell.

Why do I call this an unforced error? There's room on both sides under the shift key where another key could and should have gone, and would leave your muscle memory intact. But nah.

They also could have added more keys to the thumb clusters which, again, would have made using shortcuts a lot easier. There is no reason alt shouldn't be bilateral.

I got this thing for a smooth $80 new on craig's list. I can't recommend it. Maybe if you're mostly trying to ease pain... but not if you're a power user who is already fluent in your keyboarding ways.

title: Works incredibly well.
text:
I picked these up as dual-purpose sandbags--one use for weighting/dampening my tripod, and the other for weighting my light stand. The split-bag design works good for weighting around the light stand's feet, and the webbing strap makes it easy to put onto a tripod's center column hook. Further, the double zippers are on the "underside" and thus it's unlikely they can be opened accidentally.

As for the bags themselves, I've only had the opportunity to use them twice, so I can't comment on the longevity. As mentioned, these are indeed empty bags--you need to add ballast yourself. 1st time I used miscellaneous stuff as ballast that was lying around the house. Since I was looking for a more permanent solution, prior to the second time, I bought a 50lb bag of playground sand at a local home improvement store, and filled the bags to 20lbs, 15lbs, 10lbs, and 5lbs respectively since I wanted options.

For filling these, you'll want some other bag if you use granular ballast--like sand. The zippers aren't a hermetic seal. Your typical ziplock bag will work fine. Since the bags have 2 compartments you'll want to split the weight for each side. I was meticulous, using a scale to weigh out everything (i.e. for the 20lb bag fling up 2 ziplock bags with 10lbs of sand each), but I don't think you need to be as meticulous as I was.

A ziplock bag, filled with 10lbs of sand (with the air evacuated as best as I could will just barely fit into a pocket--with a little maneuvering. Thus, it's safe to say that a bag will carry 20lbs of weight. The straps don't seem strained and the zippers with a bit of maneuvering will indeed close tight. Overall the weight was 20lbs and a couple of ounces for the heaviest one.

Since I didn't want to overload my tripod for the 2nd time I used a bag (I had a large long lens attached to the tripod for the eclipse), I opted for the 5lb bag. Even 5lbs was able to dampen the tripod well enough in spite of the wind that accompanied the eclipse. I could have gone heavier for more dampening, but I didn't want to risk overloading the tripod.

Overall, I'd say these are a great buy. Yeah, you need to do some of the prep work yourself, but I think this is minor. I'd highly recommend.

this is going to be a quick review, because i dont have much to say. i had originally wanted this monitor, but had to get the AOC Q2963PM 29-inch, instead (i missed a sale that made them the same price). well the aoc was broken and i i was able to return it for this one.

anyway...this monitor is freaking GREAT! im coming from 2 19 inch widescreens....and wow...what a difference.

its beautiful right out of the box and i didnt feel the need to mess with any of the settings. i will say...its a bit bright to start...might be too bright for some but i like it.

im giving it 4 stars instead of 5 because the positioning of the inputs is really stupid...and theres a piece that sticks out of the back, both of which makes flush mounting to a wall difficult to impossible (depending on which inputs you use). you can not flush mount with a non adjustable vesa mount at all using the dvi input (which is what i wanted to do), as the port is rear facing causing the cable to stick out almost an inch past the back of the monitor. i had to use the hdmi port, which is side facing to get it flush.

other than that annoyance this monitor is spectacular. some places will list it as 14ms refresh and some will list it as 5ms...well its 5ms grey to grey...which i think is the case for most if not all of the monitors in this class. either way...ive been gaming on it and can say i do not notice any ghosting whatsoever....but ymmv.

i see people knocking it a little because not all games support the format...well thats not the monitors fault, besides...all the games will work, they just might not fill the entire screen...again...not the monitors fault.

i primarily use my computer for general web surfing, a little gaming, and most importantly music production. the 2560x1080 resolution is somewhat narrower than the 2880x900 i was using with the 2 19inch monitors....but the extra vertical space, no break in the middle, and just plain larger size makes this far superior to my old setup.

i would highly recommend this to anyone looking to upgrade to the 21:9 format.

title: How to assemble!!
text:
I consider myself an assembly nerd. I love assembling IKEA, Amazon, EQ3 furniture...whatever. I don't know why. I might need counseling.

So when I saw the parts for this, it looked insanely easy. I thought I'd be done in 5 minutes. 30 minutes later, I was scratching my head and reading reviews to see if I was missing something. But then, I finally solved the riddle.

So here's the deal...it IS very easy to assemble (and all my parts were in the box). What they ignorantly fail to tell you is: when you install the "upper" legs into the top shelf, *do not tighten all the way*. Tighten about 50-75% so there's plenty of wiggle. You'll need them to spread out to fit the sockets in the bottom shelf.

Then, screw the bottom legs in - via the bottom shelf - into the top legs. Once the bottom legs are screwed into the top legs, go back and tighten the top legs all the way. You'll probably need to tighten the bottom legs again after that.

It's amazing they leave that detail out in the instructions. If you tighten them all the way, they don't come close to matching up with the pre-drilled holes and you're left wondering if you have a defective product.

Once everything was assembled it worked great. No wobbles, as some report. It is smaller than I anticipated....doesn't hold all our records. But it'll do.

title: Great for remote control of a still camera. Not great for filming.
text:
[[ASIN:B016V1G9J2 Movo Photo MGB-5 Aluminum Motorized 360° Pan / Tilt Gimbal Head for Tripods & Jibs - Supports Cameras up to 11 LBS]]

My intention was to use this to film youth and high school football games. Based on the price and the look of it I thought it would be a good fit. I read the reviews and watched videos of it in action. The only thing that stuck in my mind was the separate speed control for movement. That should have told me it wasn't going to work for what I needed.

Pros:
- Well built. Good solid materials packaged well.
- Holds the weight it says it does.

Cons:
- Sliders move while you're tightening the knob down (mentioned in an earlier review)
- Upper gear has play in it. Not an issue for most. Depends on your intended use.
- Motors can be awkward to install
- Motors are noisy
- Control box is well built, but heavy and uncomfortable to hold for extended periods.

The main cons for me are the controls and the motors.

First the motors. I would think that stepper motors would give more precise control over the movement, and have a wider speed range. The slowest setting on this was pretty slow, but the fastest wasn't really fast enough to keep up with a football traveling down field after a kick. A couple of small stepper motors like you would see in a 3D printer would work well for this.

Looking at the joystick you can tell it's attached to a potentiometer for each axis, yet the designers chose to use those as on/off switches to control motor direction. If they had used the potentiometers in their circuit to control the speed of the motors directly making it so you can move the axis faster or slower depending on how far you push the stick in that direction, then this would have truly been a fantastic product.

An example would be the kickoff. You want to be able to pan very quickly, but tilt very slowly to follow the ball down field. The way this is currently set up the pan and tilt motors will always go the same speed. It may just be me, but I can't think of a filming situation where this kind of movement would really work well.

Bottom line, if all you need to do is remotely control the position of a camera to take a snapshot, then this will work great for you. If you are filming something and need remote pan and tilt, this probably isn't what you're looking for.

I give it 3 stars because they built a solid product, but didn't take it that one step further to make it a great one.

At the lowest setting it's very low but after a minute amount of increase in the dial (like 1mm), it goes to full volume. So I returned it and ordered a second one, hoping the issue would not repeat. Unfortunately, I had exactly the same issue!!! I contacted DoukAudio about the problem and they very quickly responded with instructions to remove two resistors from the circuit board. Pretty easy if you have a soldering iron. And once the resistors are removed, the product started to work perfectly, as per the product description. Long story short, I ended up being very happy with the product and DoukAudio's customer service, but I have to deduct one star because of the hassle. title: Great sound, features, and price!
text:
I've always been a fan of Alpine products. Sound quality has always been superb, and even seem to hold up years after the fact to compete with newer tech that comes out from competitors. If you want great sound quality, Alpine has always been a solid choice. Problem is, Alpine can be expensive.
Well, this unit surprised me. The sound quality is great, typical of a brand I've come to love and enjoy. What gets me is the features for the price though. For the first time in my life I have a bluetooth stereo system in my car, and I'm so spoiled I can't ever go back! Pairing was simple and quick, and now I don't even have to take out my phone. I hop in the truck and start driving, it will sense my iphone and automatically start playing whatever I was listening to last, even if spotify is closed. No more auxiliary cable!! No more alternator whine!! I can charge my phone and play music at the same time without interference, which is truly a gift to be cherished. Thank god for bluetooth! At this price point too, it's almost too good to be true. When I get my other truck back on the road again, this will be going in that vehicle too.
For those of you without bluetooth, or who don't like the automatic playback idea (I'm sure there is a setting you can change but I like it so I didn't bother looking) this comes with an aux and USB input, and there is an option to purchase satellite radio and use this as a receiver. There are plenty of inputs and outputs in the back too, for those with a more advanced setup with amps and subwoofers. For those of you who like to customize things, you can choose the color of the display and the text. Another really awesome feature is blackout, so you aren't blinded by head unit lighting late at night.
I would strongly recommend this unit for your vehicle, I've been extremely happy with mine so far!
