title: Great for travel and heavy phone users.
text: My youngest sister lives on her phone.  I don't think her battery is ever full, even when it's on the charger over night it just never seems to get fully charged at all.  Don't get me wrong, its nothing wrong with her phone but it's her heavy usage that's the culprit.  I wanted to get this charger for my phone but decided to get it for my sister instead.  The case arrived in standard packaging and was easy to remove.  I would recommend charging up the case first before putting it on your phone for the first time.  Attaching it to the phone is very easy.  Simply slide your phone onto the charging pin in the case.  You will have to remove the top half of the case to connect your phone, once it's connected snap back on the top half of the case and you're ready to go.  When your phone is running low on battery press the power button on the back of the phone to turn on and start the charging process.  You'll know your phone is charging when the lighting bolt shows next to the battery like it does when connected to your wall charger.  Once your battery case is connected you don't have to remove it for charging, simply charge the case, make sure it's powered on so it charges your phone fully as well.  When charging with the case, charging time is increased.  The case does add to the overall weight of your phone, however it's not too heavy.  The case does not interfere with the flash so you don't have to worry about how your photo will look.  Overall it's been a great case for my sister.  Now she has double the battery life when she's out and her phone stays charged up a lot longer than it did in the past.  I would highly recommend this product to anyone who needs the extra battery.  I would also recommend adding a screen protector on your phone as well.

title: A decent running watch:  HR fairly accurate, accelerometer a pain point
text:
I've owned the watch for about 3 weeks now and wanted to post an initial review. I will update this as I use the watch more.

Summary: it's a good watch - but just okay. it has some obvious accuracy issues. Garmin support has been pretty unhelpful so far.

Pros:
- Snug, comfortable fit - I've never worn a wrist strap quite like this; it's very well made. It is stretchy, soft, pliable plastic that grips tightly in heavy sweat.
- The watch interface is easy and intuitive
- The controls are straightforward and easy to learn
- Overall the construction and quality of the mechanics are top notch; the watch is very light
- Built-in HR has been fairly accurate in my experience, despite what other reviewers have noted - but YMMV
- GPS signal acquisition is very fast, even in rural areas; less than 30 seconds
- GPS measurements seem fairly accurate for outdoor activities

Cons:
- Accelerometer - by far the biggest let down for this device, as you can see from Garmin's own support article here: https://support.garmin.com/support/searchSupport/case.faces?caseId=%7B8fc7d8e0-6676-11e3-f27b-000000000000%7D; basically, Garmin removed the ability to manually calibrate the accelerometer (a feature present on older watch versions) and the watch will arrive to you uncalibrated and inaccurate. The _only_ way to calibrate the device is to run outdoors - an option that might not be available to you in the dead of winter. Therefore, if you got this watch for christmas, you might not be able to use it for 5 months. Luckily there was some warm weather recently and I was able to get in about 6 outdoor runs (which meets the minimum number of outdoor activities required to calibrate the device, according to Garmin), but the accelerometer is still very inaccurate. It's about 30 seconds off my pace and .1 - .2 miles off distance on a typical 3-mile treadmill run indoors. Luckily, you can edit your workouts after they post to Garmin Connect and correct the distance inaccuracy.
- Watch face is larger than digital display area
- Workflow is a bit clumsy and repetitive - you have to synch the watch to the phone which then beacons out to their cloud service; to update the device, you tether it to your computer. seems like you're always jumping back and forth between the app on your phone, the garmin connect app on your PC for synching and the Connect website for stats. They need to consolidate this and make it easier. The only app I want to use is the cloud one - I shouldn't have to jump through the other two apps all the time. The cloud interface comes with a lot of bloatware features that I don't find useful, and it's not possible to customize most of this. I've also found it to take several seconds to load the page.
- Some customization/quick-use features are lacking on the watch itself - such as hotkey button presses for switching GPS/bluetooth on and off (very useful if you run indoors frequently)
- The bluetooth connection is a bit flaky; if you're exercising with a separate bluetooth device such as headphones for music, I've found that the Garmin watch will suddenly connect/disconnect 5-6 times in a row at various points in my workout, buzzing me each time. Very glitchy.
- Support has been pretty awful - after 2 days waiting for a response to my issues above, I was disappointed to receive a copy and pasted text from the link above, which I already mentioned to them I had read. Then they asked questions that were clearly already answered in my original text. Pretty lazy and unhelpful support so far, but maybe that will change after I post enough mediocre reviews on various social media websites.

title: Great design/features and decent sound but overambitious touch controls with a potential fatal flaw.
text:
I had high hopes for these headphones as I needed a good set of cans for my commute. I had really grown accustomed to entry-level "audiophile" over-ear headphones like the Audio Technica M50x but despite their decent passive noise isolation, ambient noise in the subway or walking across the George Washington Bridge sometimes drowned them out. I wanted a set of more portable, wireless, noise-canceling headphones and read that these struck a good balance. I did not expect audiophile quality sound. So let me break it down by categories:

Sound (3-4/5): Decent. These are not "audiophile" grade by any means. They are pleasant, warm, easy to listen to (not fatiguing), better than most ear buds, decent bass (though it can overlap with low mids), and with the equalizer can be customized a bit to fit your preference. But compared to audiophile grade they are not as detailed or clear. Still, for a set of active noise canceling headphones loaded with features, it's a good enough sound for a commute.

Noise-canceling (4/5): Very good. In some settings it is really impressive and makes the whole world seem to disappear. Obviously it can't block out unpredictable transient sounds and it won't completely eliminate very loud low frequency rumbles (like the subway) but certainly dampens them impressively. One disappointment is its handling of wind noise. Wind sometimes seems to feed into the headphones. I think this is because the microphones are picking up the wind and failing at canceling it (so it ends up getting transmitted into the headphone). It's not a fatal flaw and typically not a major problem unless the wind is really strong. But this is the reason ANC doesn't get 5/5.

Build (4/5): Although it initially feels like a plastic toy I grew to like the build over the time. It is light and sleek. Nothing much to say about it. I suspect durability could be an issue but haven't had them long enough.

Comfort (5/5): I thought they were very soft and comfortable. Not too much clamping force.

Controls (2/5): This is the potential fatal flaw. I would have given this a 1/5 but I do like the concept of the touch controls and when they are working well it is very convenient. I wouldn't have minded occasional hiccups but here is where the real issue. On cold and/or windy days, the touch controls were spontaneously activate. This would cause voice assist to activate randomly or tracks to pause/skip. It made the headphones unusable outdoors on cold and/or windy days. In addition, a few times the controls stopped working, then became fritzy. I had to turn off/on the headphones to get them to work. This was the most disappointing issue the headphones had. Many people will want them for commuting which for many involves being outdoors. This problem essentially renders them unusable for this application. In normal indoor environments (or airplanes I suspect) they work well.

Other features/misc (5/5): Loaded with neat features (some useful, some fun). Decent phone app with equalizer. Interesting ANC optimization and settings (though sometimes don't work that great). Great foldability and semi-rigid case make them very portable.

Overall (3/5): Great for indoor use or warm climates but potentially fatal flaw for those hoping to use them to commute in cold weather. I will likely have to return them. Also be aware that fakespot.com grades the reviews with an "F" suggesting high deception is involved (in contrast to the "A" that the Bose QC 35 II have). I will may try the Bose QC 35 II despite possibly inferior sound given they have physical controls, are said to be more comfortable, ANC not affected by wind as much, and are also foldable and portable. Alternatively, I may stick to my M50x or M50xBT or Sennheiser 598cs for better sound quality but no ANC. The ATH-MSR7 is an intriguing possibility given it combines audiophile level sound with active noise canceling (but I haven't loved the sound signature).

title: A stellar performer and outstanding first-effort from Kenwood! Not perfect, but top of its class.
text:
I installed this unit in a 2009 Pontiac Solstice GXP. Since this is a convertible, I have a couple issues that hard-top users may never have.

First thing's first. It's a great unit. The sound quality is fantastic. Someone mentioned that HD Radio sounds better than SiriusXM and I have to agree, and I even installed a new SiriusXM receiver, bypassing the factory one so I could use the stock antenna. The built-in crossovers and EQ are top-notch and I'm getting some incredible audio. I also installed a backup camera and the parking assist lines are easily configured to your particular needs. Image quality is lovely on that. I have an iPhone 5s and CarPlay works quite well. Occasionally I'll run into weird little hiccups with the screen being blank or music not starting unless I start it from the phone, but this is likely CarPlay software which is on the phone and not the unit itself. But 99% of the time, it's smooth sailing. A note on the screen, yes it is resistive, but don't let that be a deal-breaker. It's an extremely sensitive and accurate screen, and the contrast is decent. Of course you aren't going to get those inky blacks of a capacitive screen, but at least it does resist fingerprints and glare better. And you can use it while wearing gloves. Performance is excellent as well and I have not noticed a single hiccup in speed or menu transitions at all. This is because the Kenwood uses a tablet processor; a first of its kind in a car head unit.

A few neutral points: The unit is pretty deep. I had to completely cut out the panel behind the radio in order to get it to fit. Of course, this will depend on your vehicle. While the unit has a motorized display that can be preset to be at many different angles depending on your ride, it does not provide forward tilt. This is bit unfortunate in my case because my dash is tilted back and as I said before, it's a convertible. My screen washes out very easily during the day. Being able to tilt the screen forward so it is completely vertical would help. The screen is fairly bright, but it really should go brighter. When my top is up or I'm at low speeds, Siri works great. Unfortunately, with the top down it's pretty worthless and there's no control within CarPlay to adjust the sensitivity or noise reduction of the mic. There is in the Kenwood interface during Bluetooth calls, though.

And the bad: I mentioned the screen could be brighter, but really it should also get much dimmer. Its dimmest setting is still far too bright when you're driving at night in unlit areas. I end up manually turning off the screen by holding down one of the hard buttons below the screen. Note that if you install a backup camera and you don't have it wired to automatically power on/off with the reverse control, you have to assign the camera on/off to this button. You have to choose whether to have a backup camera or be able to turn off your screen. You can't have both. It's not the worst, but the Kenwood UI is ugly and dated. But that's the entire industry for you. Pretty much every brand has a native UI that looks like it was designed in 1998 for adolescent boys. At least some customization is available. Kenwood support even told me how to change the startup screen using a .txt file and a very specifically formatted .bmp image file.

For anyone debating between the DDX9902S and the DDX9702S, it is absolutely not worth saving the $50 for the lower model. At all. The extra $50 in the DDX9902S is well-worth it for the additional year of warranty alone even if you don't care about high-end audio. On top of that, you get the better 5v pre-outs (instead of 4v), a 7-band EQ (instead of 5-band), and a few other advanced audio features.

title: Samsung 55" LED 120hz Smart TV
text:
Okay, let me start this review by saying i'd consider myself somewhat of a tech guru and i'm also a big fan of Samsung products so my expectations of this TV were extremely high as I've always had good luck with every product I've purchased from them which includes cell phones, laptops, and other TV's. Also, I purchased this TV to replace my Top of the line 8500 Series 42" Plasma TV in the living room and that TV has an absolutely stunning picture; in 2012 I paid about $1700 for it (further hiring my expectations of this LED TV). With that being said I'm going to try and be as in-depth as I can in this review because I read a lot of negative reviews that I'd like to address with my experience.

First off, the Shipping (I know this has nothing to do with the product itself but it seems to be something a lot of people worry about and dwell on)
-Like most Amazoner's I was a bit nervous purchasing a $700 TV online, not because of Amazon but because of the possibility of it getting damaged in transit and then having to go through the whole return & replacement process. But the TV arrived in two days from time of purchase (Amazon Prime) via FedEx and the box was in perfect condition, the same as you would expect when purchasing from best buy. As I un-boxed the TV everything was good and the TV was protected with Styrofoam as well as a plastic sleeve covering the base and screen. There was absolutely no scratches or cracks on the screen or any other part of the TV and honestly it would have to be a pretty rough ride for that to happen as the TV is secured in the center of the box by the Styrofoam but these things happen. Before I mounted the TV above the fireplace in place of the old one I wanted to plug it in and make sure the picture and everything was functioning how it should, when I plugged it in it went through the installation process connecting to the internet and updating. Directly after that I went to the Netflix app and that's when I noticed that there was a dead pixel center left. This isn't a huge deal and is in no way a bad reflection on Amazon or Samsung, these things happen (a year ago I bought a laptop from best buy and got it home and it had several dead pixels). This is really the nature of the beast when dealing with electronics and is more of a quality control problem than anything.

Performance & Picture
-Now aside from the pixel issue (which is only noticeable on dark screens) this TV performs like a top of the line LED. The picture is stunningly clear and smooth, the colors are extremely vibrant, and the blacks are exceptionally deep especially for an LED. When it comes to the hertz of this TV I have had absolutely no problems with shadowing or blurring during fast action sequences so I can say it is actively 120hz. I use my TV's for a wide assortment of things, I watch a lot of Sports, play video games, and watch a lot of movies so picture and sound are extremely important aspects for me. This TV performs, I put it to the test with 1080p football games as well as first person shooters on the PS4 and I was extremely pleased. When watching sports I'd suggest turning on the "Sports Mode" too, this further optimizes the picture as well as the Audio. Like other reviews have said The factory settings for the picture will need some tuning (factory is a bit dark) depending on how you like it, I like the dynamic setting with the brightness up but that's all a matter of personal preference. Also, Samsung had a real problem with the 2013 &14 Smart Software in terms of freezing and lag, I can say without a doubt that these have been solved with the latest Smart Hub updates. Keep in mind that this TV doesn't have the Dual Core Processor like the models above it but it is quite snappy when searching the internet browser or opening up your Netflix apps. A lot of other TV Brands have done away with incorporating a web Browser in their iOS and I'm pleased that Samsung has kept it because I think its a great feature. The speakers on the TV are truly impressive, the volume goes 0-100 and in my fairly large living room I would never need it about 40. I was listening to Sirius radio and had it on 75 and it was clear and loud for a TV. Also the pre-programmed Audio settings are great, generally they really don't do much when you put it on "clear voice" or "Movie" but with this TV you can hear a noticeable difference. My favorite aspect of this TV is that it can Identify and open my 2TB Seagate desktop HDD. Now, this is great for people like me who have a ton of videos, movies, pictures and other media on an external HDD and want to be able to open and access it in one spot for a true multimedia center. My other TV did not have the capability to read this, but this smart TV not only reads it but it has all the codecs to be able to play a wide range of media; So with 2 USB ports you can plug in 2 thumb drives or HDD's and switch between them by pressing the Source button on the remote. Lastly, I had read a few reviews about how terrible the viewing angle on this TV was and the fact that it could only be viewed from certain angles, I really don't understand this. I have this TV mounted on a telescopic full motion articulating mount that can go in just about every possible position and I put the TV in the most skewed positions (positions no one would ever watch TV in) and it was just the same as perfectly level. I saw absolutely no difference in picture quality or anything else. I can imagine that in some of those positions there might be a problem with glare in high lighting rooms but that's not the TV's fault.

If I had to have a complaint
--If i had to have a complaint it would be that the TV is fairly thick for a 2015 TV. We have come to expect everything to be as thin as possible with today's technology but this really doesn't bother me, id rather have something with a little substance and built solid. However, for someone that low profile is their number one they may want to look elsewhere. And when I say thicker, I mean about 3 1/2 inches -- the TV is light in weight though. Also, the remote is very simple, I would have enjoyed a TV remote much like the one that comes with Vizio's 70" TV with the built in QWERTY keyboard but oh well. Finally, the HDMI situation, like others have stated this TV does only have 2 HDMI ports, which is a bit disappointing because if your like me you like to have your cable or satellite box, your PS4 or Xbox, and an HDMI cord running to your laptop plugged in all at once. It's inconvenient but it is easily fixed. All you have to do is buy a 3 or 4 port HDMI switch that automatically senses which port has a signal for 10$ here on Amazon. This TV only having two HDMI ports should in no way deter your from buying it, especially when there is such an inexpensive easy fix.

Return & Replacement
-Because of the Dead pixel I obviously had to contact Amazon for a replacement. Now instead of going through the online process I called Amazon's Award winning customer service to talk with a Rep Directly. Keep in mind this TV was delivered on a Friday at about 3PM, I called customer service at about 7pm and after talking with them briefly they issued me a replacement and had it ordered in about 20 Minutes. Within that time I was emailed a packing slip and a shipping label to attach to the box. Amazon then arranged for UPS to come to my house and pick up the TV for return. This worked out great because Monday morning UPS delivered the replacement and picked up the damaged one. I mean honestly, what else could you ask for from a company that deals with online products, they go above and beyond what anyone else in the industry is doing and they truly strive to keep there customers happy and coming back. I will choose to deal with a company like Amazon who treats you like a valued customer rather than give my business to a circus like Walmart who makes you jump through every hoop possible when returning or replacing an item every time.

I highly recommend this TV for anyone who is looking for a Mid Level priced LED TV that performs like the top classed models. This is a great choice if your not quite ready to spend the money to make the jump to 4K and I can't imagine the 60 or 65" TV's in this class perform any different.

title: A great little grab and go telescope that will always impress!
text:
This is a great telescope for anyone who just wants one to grab and go or even for everyday use.

There are three versions of the short tube 80MM that Orion sells. The OTA (Optical Tube Assembly) only, the A astronomical, and the T terrestrial versions. OTA only is obviously the least expensive. The astronomical version comes with a standard vixen dovetail mount, and a finder scope as well as a star diagonal. The terrestrial comes with a correct image finder and diagonal.

The ST80 is a fairly fast F5 scope. What this means is the telescope will give brighter views than say a slower F12 or even F7 telescope at a trade off of magnification. You will be able to see dimmer objects find things easier with this scope. This scope even with the provided Orion Plossl eyepieces you will be able to easily resolve four of Jupiter's moons, the whispyness of the Orion nebula will be visible and the Pleiades will be breathtaking! For visual observation you won't always want magnification. The Pleiades will look great with this scope especially with the low power eyepiece. Where you may only see one or two stars with the unaided eye you will see a dozen or in the eyepiece depending on where you look.

The ST80 is also a great size for a guide scope, not too heavy, and with good light gathering ability especially compared to the 50mm's often used with auto guiders such as Orions SSAG. (Star Shoot Auto Guider)

title: Decent sound quality, reduces cable mess
text:
WARNING: Make sure you pull out the microphone before inserting into your car stereo! It got stuck in mine.

Adapter got stuck in my tape deck and had a heck of a time getting it back out. I didn't expect any issues with this since my old-school wired tape adapter didn't have any problems ejecting from my deck. Ended up having to use a pocket knife and a small, flat screwdriver to slowly and gingerly wiggle it out of my deck. That was after I had to pull the fuse for the radio because the tape deck kept trying to pull the tape back in and then partially eject it over and over again. After I finally got it out of the tape deck, I pulled out the microphone and re-inserted it (I *really* wanted this to work, so I gave it another shot). Now, I just have to gently pull on the mic cable to get it to fully eject from the deck, but that's better than wrestling with a knife/screwdriver combo.

It also doesn't seem to be charging (or maybe it doesn't give any indication it's charging?). I figured right out of the box, it wouldn't have a full charge, so I'm surprised it didn't start charging. Plugging in the USB adapter didn't cause any lights to come on. I'll update the review once I know more.

As far as operation goes, it seems to work as intended. Leaving the switch off as recommended, it does turn itself on automatically when the tape deck powers on, and it paired with my phone easily enough. Sound quality is decent (make sure you also remove the little piece of tape over the head as that will cause some sound degradation). Haven't used it long enough to report on the battery life.

Update: I've been using this for a month or so now, and it does seem to be charging. It lasts about 4 hours, more or less as advertised. However, I'm not sure if I got a unit that doesn't have a charge indicator light, or if it's designed without one. I also lightly sanded the outside of the case and it seems to eject from the tape deck without requiring me to gently tug the mic cable. I've updated the review to four stars instead of two.

title: Amazing glass, awesome versatility, but....

I estimate I have well over 1,000 hours behind mine, probably closer to 2,000. I hunt Coues whitetail, elk, antelope, etc...all in Arizona. On a recent scouting trip, I put these up against a pair of Vortex Kaibabs (20x) - no comparison. We have also put them head-to-head with Swarovski several times and each time, the Leica comes out a bit ahead. However, having written all that, I wish I had the 10+15x50s instead as they would give me a bit more power and I could still hand-hold at 10x, albeit not quite as steady as the 8x's (anyone out there want to trade?). Secondly, if the Lecias do not last you a lifetime, dealing with Leica is a royal pain. Swaro and especially Vortex are hands-down better on customer service. title: My cheap speakers sound better
text:
I have to say I am not very impressed by the sound quality of this device.

When I first plugged in the radio and turned it on, I was pretty un-wowed. I thought, well maybe I have set my expectations too high for such a small device, so I decided to compare the Tivoli radio with a small set of speakers that I own (link:
http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B008SE42EA?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_search_detailpage). The speakers were only $50 and are TINY (they could easily fit within the Tivoli radio) so I think it is fair to compare these devices. I performed the comparison by playing the same song on each device and switching back and forth. I did this for numerous songs and I made sure to set a similar volume on both devices. The Tivoli plays the bass range much better, which actually threw me off. For several minutes I couldn't decide why I liked the Pioneer sound so much better even though Tivoli clearly does bass better. Finally I figured it out: the Tivoli is incredibly subpar in the higher range. The Tivoli makes a singer sounds dull and lackluster, muted, muddled, almost tinny, definitely tiny. My Pioneer speakers don't do bass nearly as well, but even with that handicap it sounds better (to me) because a singer's voice comes through sharply and expressively. In addition to a person's voice, a lot of the music is played in the upper range, which also comes through crisply.

After I pinpointed the issue, I found a song with a small (if any?) bass role and asked my husband to do a blind test. I set up the devices so the sound would come from the same direction and had him close his eyes. Then I played a small sample from each speaker and asked if he could tell a difference in volume between the two devices. He could not (which is good, I didn't want one speaker to be louder than the other, that might give those speakers an advantage). Then I played the song (San Francisco by Vanessa Carlton) from each device for about 20 seconds and then started to go back and forth. He told me he didn't need to hear any more because he liked the sound of one device so much better than the other. He indicated that he liked the Pioneer speakers more. He was COMPLETELY astonished when I told him which device he had chosen.

For me that sealed the deal. The Tivoli just doesn't sound that good. It plays bass, sure, but it is lackluster in every other range range. To me, it ends up sounding pretty one-dimensional and unimpressive.

The pros are: the device is very attractive and I like the smooth feel of the dials (very nice). It also seems to pick up radio quite well. However, I bought this radio primarily for sound quality, and I did not feel it lived up to my expectations.

title: Useless amplifier, Bogus rating and reviews. Buyer beware
text:
This Antenna amplifier is not worth the effort connecting to an antenna. This product got high stars with bogus reviews. Since quite few folks gave good review, I assumed at least it should have some merits.

After checking the products with various antennas with different configurations, I went back to read reviews again. All bogus reviews. These folks got the free antenna amplifiers claimed as test and gave 5 star. I am not talking about one review, I am talking about almost all.

I went further and read these reviewers other product reviews. Same story, these are fake reviews claiming as free product. This is done to manipulate Amazon's rating system.

Now, real testing and review here for you. I have tested with two antennas, and two tuners. I did not expect too much from it or any new channels, rather I was expecting to increase signal strength on couple of channels from dropping out/pixelating when it is cloudy.

1. Tried with Antennacraft HBU22 Antenna: Connected Amplifier at LG TV and tested.
a. I took reading of Signal strength and Signal Quality for each channel before installing amplifier and after installing amplifier. Absolutely no change. I was expecting some, nope, nothing, Nada..
b. I moved the Amplifier near antenna to see if it makes difference if I put amplifier at source. Nope, Nothing changed..

2. Tried with ClearStream 4 antenna. Same steps near TV and Near Antenna. Absolutely no improvement.

Then tried two antennas with ViewTV PVR tuner. Same story, Nothing changed. No gain in signal strength.

Only merit it has is, it did not block signals, worked as 1 foot extension cable.. Nothing more.

So total 8 attempts/configurations, absolutely no improvements.

From now on "WATCH OUT FOR BOGUS REVIEWS and RATING MANIPULATIONS".

Note: These bogus reviewers are in full force trying to make my review invisible. Check my other reviews. Detailed, and useful information and most helpful reviews. Product good or bad, a review should be unbiased and should not change based on whether you got it for free or not.

title: Curved and WQHD is the way to go with a monitor
text:
I spend all day at work on spread sheets. Columns will easily go past the A-Z columns and into the AAs and beyond. Because of this I started researching for a monitor to fit my daily PC use and learned that the best resolution for wide spreadsheets is the WQHD resolution of 3440x1440 which has a 21:9 aspect ratio. So the search was on for a monitor with that resolution.

Now the sizes of monitors with the 3440x1440 resolution (WQHD) are generally in the 34”-35” range. There are 34” monitors that can be purchased between $400-600, but the new technology for this size of monitor is the CURVED display. If you are already considering a large purchase, you might as well go all out and get a curved one. That is one of the major reasons why I choose the Philips 349X7FJEW and let me tell you the curve is definitely worth it. The 1800 R curvature makes looking at the spreadsheets a lot easier on my eyes and my brain. I honestly believe it makes me more productive as I am immersed in the screen and can focus.

One of my friends got a 34” flat panel monitor. He had to set it up on a filing cabinet behind his desk because he said it was too close and too big for him. Mine is setup exactly 24” from the center of the monitor to the edge of my desk and is a perfect distance.

Since it is a curved LCD panel, the panel type is a VA. According to Philips, the VA is a “wide viewing angle” with 178 degrees of horizontal and vertical viewing angles. That is the same spec as IPS panels that are becoming more and more popular. It also has AMD Freesync technology if you are into gaming and can take advantage of the 4ms response time. Keep in mind it only has a 60Hz refresh rate.

There is an onboard LowBlue Mode setting that you can turn on by using the Joystick menu button. The LowBlue Mode reduces the amount of shortwave blue light to help your eyes. It makes the screen looked washed out, but after a long day looking a spreadsheets, it’s nice to turn it on for the last push of work before leaving the office. Other modes are FPS, Racing, RTS, Gamer1, and Gamer2.

The PROS:
WQHD Resolution and CURVED panel.
The built in speakers are great for listening to music while I work or for watching online videos.
HDMI 1.4 input (also has displayport 1.2) and 3 USB ports. I have my keyboard and external displays hooked up. 1 USB 3.0 goes to my PC and is enough to power them all.
Multiview PIP and PBP (you can have two inputs displayed at the same time, haven’t used it yet but it’s nice to know if I need it)
Height adjustment has 6” and ¼ range from all the way up to all the way down. Sometimes I’ll mix it up depending what I’m working on.
Philips has a 4 YEAR WARRANTY. Where else can you find a warranty like for electronics?

The CONS:
Futuristic looking stand doesn’t hide cables well.
Only 3 USB ports, once you get a few, you want more.
Power brick is huge, it is almost the size of an actual brick.

OVERALL:
Recommend this monitor to anyone who spends 8 hours a day on the computer. I’ve heard the new 4K monitors (that I know are sharp picture wise) make you go up and down with your head on spreadsheets. Get the curved WQHD resolution instead, it’s for the workers.

text:
I personally really like this. The price, I will admit, is a little obnoxious but 1) its Apple so what do you expect and 2) I use it quite a bit and so far I am very pleased with it. When paired with certain apps, the use of the pencil really comes into light. I'm not sure if some people would prefer their stylus to be lighter or heavier, but I prefer mine to have a little bit of weight to it. This apple pencil feels solid inside unlike other stylus pens I've used in the past.

Cons (if you are picky about these things. These aren't really things I dislike, these are more suggestions for those who are worried about these specific features of the product)

The adapter to charge could get easily lost if you dont keep track of it due to its small size (I keep everything in the box when I'm not using it because I am notorious for losing my belongings so the box is the best place for me personally)
If you dont use the adapter you CAN plug it into the port on your actual iPad, however it's very awkward with a pencil just sticking out the bottom. I dont use this method in fear that I'm gonna accidentally hit the pencil or something and ruin both the port and the actual pencil.
The cap that COVERS the lighting plug in (I have noticed) seems to bother some people due to it completely coming off when you charge it (I dont mean that it falls off on its own. The cap itself is magnetic and stays in place. I mean more in the sense of voluntarily removing the top cap to charge the Pencil). Therefore when it isnt covered, the cap is just laying around. They do have a solution for that on amazon (an atachment for the pencil to keep it attached to the pencil if you are afraid of that. (Once again, I just put it in the box. That small extra step doesnt bother me).

At first I thought there was really no way to see how much the pencil was charged, but turns out there is a widget that becomes available on your iPad that you can add to your screen to keep you in the know.

Those cons dont particularly bother me enough to rate this product bad or to purchase attachments of any sort. If you are really afraid of losing this device, they have iPad cases with places to hold your apple pencil and they even have actual Apple Pencil cases to keep your pencil in separately. And if you're worried about dropping it and it breaking or getting scratches on it,they have silicone "sleeves" for the pencil as well for extra protection.

title: Not much of an upgrade over the HD598, but still great.
text:
I received these from Sennheiser's warranty program, which is incredible I might add. To save you some time, both these and the HD598s which these replaced offer a similar quality of sound. Feel free to read more of my story below if you want more background info. Definitely recommend both these and the HD598s if you can afford them.

I originally purchased the HD 598s almost 2 years ago. Unfortunately, I have a big head and am prone to breaking headsets from constantly taking them on/off my head. This is far from the first headset to break at the hinge of the cup for me, so I don't fault them here. The HD598 soundstage is amazing. As a father and husband, an open soundstage is important to me. I also regularly broadcast on Twitch, so being able to hear my own voice accurately is a nice plus.

These headphones offer a great range of quality sound, with well-articulated bass to warm mids and highs. When I originally upgraded from mid-range headphones to the HD598, it was mind-blowing hearing accents and instruments in my favorite songs that I'd never heard before. These HD599s offer a similar experience with a better build quality. However, they are not as light as the HD598s were.

For me, the build quality is a major plus considering so many headsets have broken on me, but for the average consumer, the lighter feel of the HD598s will probably offer a better experience. In general, it feels more like "another option" than it does an upgrade over the HD598s, so I don't know that I can justify the (currently) $30 price premium for these over the HD598s. Both are great headphones either way and will continue to provide hours of joy.

title: It's working well
text:
This review is for TL-WR841N, hardware version 9.
2/13/2015: Had this router up for 1 week now. It's working good so far. Setting up the router is really easy. During day 1 it did drop the connection a few hours after it went online. Because the firmware on the unit I received was a version from 2013 so I went to tp-link's website to get the latest version. On their website, I noticed if you select the region to be Global, then you would see the latest version "TL-WR841N_V9_150104" (published on 01/04/2015), however if you select the region to be "United States", the latest version is "TL-WR841N_V9_141013" (published on 10/13/2014). I took the latest version from the US region. After the firmware update I haven't had any connection drop. The router's range is better than my old Linksys WRT54GL. This router has mixed b/g and mixed b/g/n mode but does NOT have wireless-N only mode. I heard mixed mode decreases the speed compared to wirelss-N only mode (of course assuming all of your devices are N mode compatible). But for $20, you can't really ask for more. I liked this enough that I ordered another one as a backup and possibly as an Access Point. Since this router is only 1 week old, so the 5-star is only temporary. I will post updates if things change.

2/28/2015: Had to reboot the router because a couple of devices lost connection. Router's own log wasn't helpful. Looked at Windows event log and it appears the problem might have happened when router was renewing the IP address for these devices. By the way, unlike some of the Linksys routers where you can set the lease time to infinite, this router has very short IP lease time (default is 120 minutes and max is 2880 minutes). Still looking into the problem but for now have to change it to 3 stars.

Also, for those who are thinking about installing DD-WRT on this router, it is NOT available yet for hardware version 9 of this router (most likely you will get hardware version 9 if you buy from Amazon right now). But beta versions of DD-WRT are available if you're willing to try.

5/31/2015
It has been completely trouble free since late Feb. I think it deserves a 5 star.

text:
Replacing an old Canon Pixma that has given me some issues lately. This one set up like a dream and looks great. I do NOT like the manual feed placement. IT's on the back and has no support for the paper and automatically sucks in the single sheet of paper. I worry about future jams if it sucks it in at an angle.

It's incredibly loud. I thought the other reviewers were nuts, but this is loud and gives off a high pitch whine when it's printing high quality color.

So far it seems to be using a ton of ink for me. The colors were too light to begin with, and I had to tinker with the advanced settings. The color is still off, (too dark now) but better than it was. Printing full color sheets are extremely slow. Way slower than my Canon that's nearly 10yrs old. Quality is about the same. I was expecting some sort of improvement in this area, but nope.

I'm not sure if I'm going to keep this as I use my machine to print product labels and if the colors continue to be off, I might send it back and continue fighting with my old machine that actually prints the colors reliably, even if the print heads in that one keep getting clogged (requiring me each time I change inks to run cleanining on it for 1-2hrs at a time.) So you can see why I wanted to upgrade... but if the new printer can't get the colors right I can't see keeping it.

Update: A few days out, another few cons I discovered was that the black is not liquid, it is like laser powder toner. So when printing on glossy, it will smudge incredibly easily but will dry eventually.

I'm still not 100% happy with the print quality. It's a bit blurry/pixel-y. I went from using USB to wireless and had to reinstall the software all over again to make it work, there is no quick fix when switching how it's plugged in.

At this point, it's a huge hassle to send it back, so I'm keeping it now that I have learned its quirks. But because of this I'm still keeping my old printer hooked up as well which is incredibly inconvenient.

**UPDATE**
After owning this printer for a month and using it on a daily basis, I can in fact say I regret buying it 100%. I use the rear manual feed tray quite often for glossy labels and it's incredibly difficult to load and often times loads it wrong.
Anytime I use glossy paper, everything blurs and all of the ink smudges way too easily (it even smudges hours after waiting for it to dry.) It sort of reacts like powdered toner, not liquid ink.

Sadly I got busy and missed my return window by a few days, so I cannot send it back, I am stuck with it and will only be using it for basic paper print jobs (those of which are often blurry and the colors are weird.)

title: Impressive little voice recorder, perfect for journalists
text:
I'm so impressed with this. I'm a journalist and I had always done phone interviews, where I had typed people's responses as people spoke. But I took on a different type of assignment required me to do live, in-person and man-on-the-street interviews. I don't have any experience with these little recorders but I love this thing.

It picks up intelligible speech in offices, bars, and on busy streets. Even when a person far away overhears what we're talking about and they toss in an offhanded comment, it picks it up perfectly. I've even handed the recorder to little kids and asked them to interview each other... the results are incredible. Its unobtrusive, when I start talking to people, I let people I know they're being recorded. But they forget about it within a minute or two. I get so much more out of the audio than typed interviews.

I've even submitted audio for a friend's podcast and the quality of the microphone and resulting stereo audio is really impressive for a the cheap, durable little thing that this is. I highly recommend it.

At the end of the day, I can plug it right into my Mac, charge the battery, pull the audio to my laptop, and reorganize the files that I leave on the device. Highly recommended.

title: Powerful, affordable, fast-charging, uses Li-Ion, and has a built-in X controller and receiver
text:
I got one of these flashes immediately after getting the X-Pro, several X1R modules, and two of the TT600s and loving them. I had some Altura flashes before, but found that they were extremely non-linear (it jumped 2.2 stops between 1/128 and 1/64! And 1.5 stops between 1/64 and 1/32!) and wanted to replace them.

I got this after getting the TT600 because I wanted an on-camera flash with TTL/HSS to replace my stupid Alturas.

Firstly, they seem quite linear with their power (and, by linear, I mean appropriately exponential). From 1/128 to 1/1, I measured each stop and got 0.7, 1.0, 1.0, 0.9, 1.0, 0.9, and 1.0 stop differences between each of the settings. There's a little variation here and there, but overall it's quite consistent, and some of the deviations may be measurement error. Importantly, there we none of the 2.2 stop jumps that the Altura had.

Secondly, I was getting 2s full-power recharges with its Li-Ion battery when it arrived in the mail. Note that it was not particularly well charged when it arrived (i.e. it was nearly empty) and I was getting 2s recharges. I then got 50-100 (or more?) 1/8 power flashes before it finally decided it had had enough. This was all with the mostly-empty battery as it arrived in the mail. I haven't yet used it enough to know how long the battery lasts when fully charged, but I strongly suspect I won't be disappointed.

The menu structure was a little different than the TT600, probably because it has more modes. Had to use a different button to put it in the various master/slave modes, but apart from that it was easy.

One issue I had is that it would go into a sleep mode after a while and could not be waken up remotely - you actually had to press a button on the flash to wake it up. I just found out how to change that with the TT600 while writing my review on it, and looked to find the same setting with this. The settings seems different, so I need to do a little more reading on that, but I should be able to make it work.

Overall, it's a great flash with a great battery with lots of very nice features.

title: Great case with nice durability
text:
Great case with nice durability.
I'm a college student with colors that are blue and chose this case after looking at a lot of others because of the structural design this case offers. The material is very durable as I move this case (using the box provided with it) to move from school and home often and hasn't failed once!
I enjoy the 200mm sad fan and front fan that lights up as It's just bright enough to enjoy and look at while gaming and the lights aren't distracting even when running it over night while falling asleep.

Pros
-normal/slightly bigger mid-tower case for room that allows air flow
-color and lights are bright enough that it isn't distracting when gaming
-easy to unscrew and take off both side panels
-left side panel (where you should put all your cables like my picture) has plenty of space for cables to stack up.

Cons
-could use a few more holes/openings to run cables.
-in order to get cable management the way you want it you might have to unscrew some
if not all of the case fans to make the cables reach to where you want them. (though that's also the joy of building your own PC)
-could use more room between the power supply and the MoBo to allow cables more room in case you want to have 2 Video Cards installed.

Notes
-The front of the case is simple/ annoying to take off but not too big of an issue. to go with that the front panel usb/headjack piece might be tiny bit loose so check it. if it is you will have to take off the front only a little to tighten the screws in to secure it. Easy fix but a little annoying (I assume they did it for shipping safety).
-My video card's back (where you plug in the hdmi/display/dvi cables) is slightly high to where the cable doesn't go in all the way but in the time ive had the case it hasn't been an issue. This could be the case or it might my my Mobo but it doesn't bother me as i almost didn't know about it until i played around with my hardware.

For the price it is great, however if you intend to have a lot of cables running around inside I would look for a corsair or similar brand with big and many holes to run cables. Other than that I am pleased with it.

title: It works
text:
I was nervous about ordering hundreds of dollars worth of equipment that would be protecting my home from a very new company, but it's been worth it so far.

My goals were to:
1. Have a system that provides reasonable security (my house isn't Fort Knox) that I can customize as my needs change
2. Be able to monitor the system myself but have the option for short term professional monitoring
3. Be relatively future-proofed in terms of hardware
4. Have a smart home capability (the least of my concerns, but I know I will get addicted to this part)

This was the only system I could find that satisfied all of the above, after looking at traditional options like ADT, other new security systems like Scout, and smart-home-first hubs like Samsung SmartThings. I like that Abode is a security system first, and a home automation system second. The security part works seamlessly and is very easy to set up and customize. I haven't tried to do very many automations yet, but after trying a few simple things, the capability does seem powerful.

There are quirks like insufficient documentation of components online and the lack of a user forum (but Reddit is nice), but it looks like updates are continually sent out, and I'm confident that the system will just continue to get better.

title: Fragile; poorly made; needs tape to hold battery in place; does not take batteries rechargeable only
text:
This thing has major design flaws that make it borderline trash.

I really feel like you can buy a clock radio at a thrift store that takes AA batteries, and that's more reliable for disaster prep.

The battery cover will fall off if you shake or bump the radio. It will fall off if you carry the radio in a backpack or bag of pretty much any container. The battery cover will fall off. You need to take it closed and use the tape as you latch. Peel back to open. Put more tape to close. The battery is also a rechargeable pack that you connect by plugging in a wire. If the battery cover falls off, the battery flops out.

This does not take AA nor AAA batteries. The older model did, but it looks like starting in 2017, they don't let you do batteries anymore. Bad for me, because so many kids toys take batteries that I have tons in the house in all the toddler toys.

It gets FM, AM, and the weather bands. No shortwave, which I see that some other radios have. Control for volume and station selection are good. Not overly sensitive, and actually for station select you click up to each channel so you can get right on the channel you want. Dial for going AM to FM to Weather 1, Weather 2, etc. is really badly made, and some other reviews say it broke and they are stuck with AM only. I believe it, looking at the chinsy dial. Reception is good. As good as my car radio, and old clock radio (which takes AA batteries and so is actually better for a disaster than this Red Cross one).

This is really not something you can charge a phone off of. The battery in this is not enough to fully charge a smartphone. I and husband are currently using Alcatel cheapie phones, like what Cricket give you free when you sign up. Solar charging the battery for this takes an unknowably long time. Mine arrive with two of three bars of charge. Two days in the sun, and it's still two of three bars. I think charging is good if you want to use the flashlight or radio, which I always do when a hurricane has the power (and internet) out. If you think this will run you phone, you are wrong. There are solar charging battery packs wit bigger cells that will do this.

So upset I got this. Husband wanted a different one, and I was like "internet electronics are bad quality, let's get the Red Cross one." Even though it's Red Cross, it's still a really badly made radio where I needed to take it together from day 1 . Probably going to return it, and just do without. All the newer Android phones now have FM radio built in and you use Next Radio to access it, so a bunch of battery packs will get you radio for a couple of weeks. Florida has a tax free week for hurricane prep. So upset that I bought this on tax free week, and it's so so bad quality, and I have to buy something else but it is not tax free week anymore. So incredibly upset about that.

title: Nice upgrade but does alter the sound
text:
Update after 6 months of use:
They do alter the sound way too much for my taste so removing 2 stars. The bass becomes a little too bloated and the highs peaky and dry and lose their sparkle. I tried removing the mesh completely, leaving the drivers exposed but the results were the same. I suspect this happens because of their thickness that moves the drivers much farther away from your ears and changes the geometry of the cavity. I tried the Dekoni pads, which in all fairness are 2x the price, and I am much happier now.

If you are happy with the sound of these, by all means, they are a great buy. The build quality is great for the price and the manufacturer seems like a company I would like to support. It would be interesting to see WC get the form factor closer to the dekoni pads. I suspect this will fix the issue with the sound.

Original review below
---------------------------------------------------------
The good:
-value for money
-substantially better comfort vs the original pads - softer pleather, memory foam, more room for the ears, don't make my head sweat
-little to no sound signature change vs the originals (my experience of course, YMMV)
-better noise isolation - better bass and lower listening volume

The bad(ish) - these are more of nitpicks:
-because these pads are much thicker it's harder to fold the headset and fit it in its case
-they were a little more difficult to install vs the originals.
-the shape and seams between the two pads are a little inconsistent.

The neutral:
-pleather may not last as long as real leather.

title: Google OnHub - Simple, intuitive product that delivers blazingly fast wireless internet
text:
Great product, regrettable that people reviewed it before the product was officially released. That's really the only reason the average rating is so low.

Setup -
The router works great - you plug it in, download the app, set it up via your smartphone, then it's ready to work with all your devices. The OnHub is great for the household with lots of wireless devices and Internet needs, but without the normal complications and tech savvy requirements of setting up an expensive router.
App -
The Google On app is really intuitive, and allows you to adjust many settings that would only be available via your desktop and an Ethernet cable. You can prioritize a device (like an Amazon Fire Box that is streaming a movie) for a set period of time, share your network, run diagnostics, and adjust settings all with a touch of your thumb. It also has easy troubleshooting and links to websites built into the app.
Speeds -
No complaints here. All around the house, the unanimous feedback is that this router is significantly faster than our old router, and its internal speed test as well as speedtest.net both agree. The signal is strong regardless of the location of your device, and the Internet is snappy.
Ethernet -
The OnHub is built to do one job and do it well, which is provide fast wireless signal and coverage. It only has one Ethernet port, but it's not really an issue since the majority of devices can connect wirelessly nowadays. If you really need more than one Ethernet port for your old devices, you can buy a network switch for $10 on Amazon and it'll do the job.

Conclusion -
It does everything a $200 wireless router is supposed to, but without the complicated setup or troubleshooting that's usually required. Plug it in, download the app, and let it do what it's good at. Plus, it looks cool.

title: Sennheiser 650 owner...moved up to the 700s. DON'T HESITATE
text:
So I've been a proud lover of my Sennheiser 650 HDs for over 6 years. They're well worn in and I love(d) them. I ran them through a Schitt Asgard 2 headphone amp and they sounded wonderful.

So I was hesitant to mess with what I thought was perfection. I needn't have worried. The 700s, though only about $100 more on sale at amazon SOUND like the $900 headphones they're retailed at. There is a rule of thumb in headphone buying regarding the law of diminishing returns. After you spend a certain amount, the sonic improvement you're getting may pale in comparison to extra money you're shelling out. But because I got these for only around $100 more than the 650s, I took the plunge.

I run these through my same Schitt amp. Though, I do have to note that because their impedance is less than the power hungry 650s, they sound pretty darn great just plugged directly into my iPod (you'll need an adaptor for the plug as it doesn't come with the smaller one--I forgot the size--which fits iPods, laptops, etc.) These headphones are just BETTER. Better in so many ways. They're INCREDIBLY comfortable. While the 650s have a VERY tight clamp pressure, the 700s feel secure but almost weightless. I frequently forget I have them on. The sound!!! My goodness, the sound. While the 650s are often commended for being so "neutral," after hearing the 700s, the 650s sound boring and flat to me. I'm not a crazy audiophile in terms of being able to talk about all the intricate details of treble, mids, and such. Here's what I CAN say with confidence---the best part of these phones is the MASSIVE soundstage. What I mean by that is that the music just sounds...well, huge. Like you're on stage with the band and the music is surrounding you. I listened to everything from Michael Jackson to Mastodon...Miles to Mahler, and everything just sounds fabulous. Yes, you get that same amazing detail you get with the 650s, but it's not the detail that will blow you away. It's the closeness of the music. Dylan singing DIRECTLY into my ear.

So I sold the 650s.

There is one negative. I can live with it. It was pointed out by other reviewers. The cord stinks. Not in terms of sound; it gets kinked almost constantly. This doesn't affect the sound (at least to these ears), but it's a pain to keep straightening it out which I feel obsessive about doing. The folks at Sennhesier are such amazing engineers; I have no idea how this detail slipped past them but alas.

Get them.

title: Cut my max load temperatures down by 30C vs stock 4790k!!!
text:
I bought this to replace the stock fan on my 4790k. I was having some semi-severe temperature issues when using TurboBoost (up to 4.4 ghz) and fully loading the processor to near 100% at 1.260V. I was reaching temperatures as high as 95C, to which I immediately ended the load to avoid severe damage. Needless to say, the stock cooler is NOT a practical solution for running clocks & voltages this high. I turned off TurboBoost in the BIOS, which caps the processor to 4.0 standard clock speeds, but also lowers the max voltage to about 1.15. This voltage decrease keeps the temperatures lower - But why have an unlocked powerhouse processor that I have to baby with the stock cooler?

Enter the NH-D14. Installation wasn't 'easy', but it wasn't hard either. The instructions come in separate books for AMD/Intel. Per the instructions, I removed my motherboard, installed the backplate (fairly simple), and installed the new cooler mounting brackets on the opposite side. It does give you layouts for the final product in the instructions. I chose to have mine intake on the side closest to the drive bays, and exhaust on the opposite side, facing the rear case fan (both fans are moving air in the same direction, on opposite sides of the sinks). I believe this is going to be the most efficient way to install in 90% of applications.

The absolute most difficult portion of installing this sink is finding the space for it. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS COOLER IF YOU'RE RUNNING ANYTHING SMALLER THAN ATX MOTHERBOARD, AND MID-ATX CASE. I am running a standard mid size atx, and standard atx board. I had enough room to get everything installed, but the high heat sinks on my Corsair Vengeance RAM posed an issue and I will be replacing the memory rather than voiding my warranty by removing the sinks. One last point of advice is do not try to install the cooler whilst your board is outside your case. I didn't try this, but I seriously doubt it will work. While it's harder to fit your hands into the nooks and crannies in the case, it will be best.

The fans are both removable, and are adjustable vertically due to the neat brackets. You can even flip them rather than the sink, if you desire a different airflow configuration. If for whatever reason you prefer to have just one fan (or can only fit one) you can easily remove one and use it as a 140MM case fan. You may also remove and use your own fans if you don't like the look of these, but I'd imagine these are going to be quieter than most fans you'd get, and you may have a hard time with the bracket system.

On to the fun stuff: My temperatures were DRASTICALLY improved. My idle temps pre install were 35C or so (with turbo boost & speedstep ON). Post install, my idle temps were often down as low as 22C (below my room temperature), but varied between 22-26C. Under load, with stock cooler and the above settings still on, as mentioned, I was seeing temperatures as high as 95C. With the new cooler installed, I'm able to sustain 4.4 GHZ @ 100% load for forever and the temps never go over 70, and typically sit between 60-65C. All of this testing was done in a home with an ambient temperature of 22.2C (72F). See pictures for my proof!

This is not a paid review (see verified), but is an honest opinion on this product. I can't imagine there is anything better. I just wanted to inform everyone about how amazing this cooler is.

title: The pink one is not pink enough, but otherwise an awesome product
text:

I am an artist and technologist so I love fun colors on technology. I would have tried the blue one, but it was out of stock so I ordered the pink one. + The no-roll case is definitely a plus since we take the tap all over the house with us and can lay it down in any direction.
+ The bottom edge doesn't hinder the connection to the charging cradle.
+ Snug fit; No fear of the device slipping out.
+ No (noticeable) impact to audio quality.
+ Sleek and sexy.
+ Easy to clip to your backpack, purse, belt loop, 24K chain, whatever
+ I haven't noticed anything 'sticking' to the sling's material. It's remained pretty clean! No dust or grime.
+ Better price point than the $20 Amazon sling.
- The colors aren't as fun as Amazon's version of the sling.

title: Cool idea - Not so exellent execution
text:
A nice device, perfect for reading books. With that said, there are some issues. One, the magnets are not strong enough on the external battery/ cover. The first day I had it I picked up the kindle off the table, the battery/ cover fell off and got chipped on one edge. The weak magnets are also constantly causing the kindle to say the attached battery/ cover is not supported.

Next, if you turn the brightness down during daytime use and then come back and try to use with little to no light available you cannot see enough to turn the brightness up. They really should have made this automatically turn the brightness to 6 or 7, for 30 second or so, when the device wakes up.

Once in a while, when changing pages using the touch screen, it gets stuck in the last mode to used. Meaning, if you go forward a page and then try to go back a page it just keeps going forward, and vise versa.

Another issue, there is no way to return/ delete, unwanted/ read, free and borrowed books directly from the kindle. This means you have to log into your account via the web page in order to do so, or else leave them cluttering up your Library. You can remove them from the device to free up space but they still stay listed in your Library. Plus, it's just terribly inconvenient to have to login to the website to return books when it would be simple for them to add this feature to the kindle.

Speaking about space. The Oasis supposedly has 4GB of storage and can hold thousands of books. I have 12 books in my Library and only have 2GB of available space...?

Perhaps my biggest complaint however is, even though we payed $298 for a device that, technologically speaking, is worth less than half that, they force you to pay another $20 dollars to have the "Special Offers" removed. With the price of the device and the cost of books and/ or kindle service you would think this would be a settings option and not a pay to remove item!

title: Best Gaming Headphones I've Owned!
text: After having experienced many other gaming headsets, ranging from Astro A40/50, SteelSeries H Wireless, and Turtle Beach Elite 800; I would have to say that these are the cleanest sounding headphones I've used. The sound detail is very clear, you can hear the subtle details in the environment, and the positional audio is on-point. I'm currently using this in conjunction with the Astro Mixamp TR and it's a very good combo for a desk gaming setup. These headphones are pretty comfortable, once you make a few adjustments on the placement of the wings on your head. These headphones doesn't need any additional amplifiers as the Mixamp can power these just fine. The microphone on these is also crystal clear on the receiving end. I do find that the inline mute is a bit finicky but... It works. There's also a subtle click sound when you flick the mute on/off. The inline mute also has a small volume rocker which I tend to hit on accident when I mute myself. Overall, I would definitely recommend these headphones over the other gaming headsets. I'm pretty sure you also go cheap by purchasing the Audio-Technica AD900x and a ModMic 4.0, but having it all in one is nice. It all depends on your budget.

text: I have the Canon 6D, and up till now was carrying around my Tamron 24-70 f/2.8 and Canon 70-200 f/2.8 for even casual photo taking because there wasn't really a good option for me out there that I liked or wanted to spend money on. That is, until I found this. I can't believe I didn't notice this lens sooner. It's proving to be something I'm enjoying shooting with a lot! I had to micro adjust the tele end to -5, but the wide end I left at zero. I can say that doing some photo tests I found it pretty sharp at 28mm, a bit back focused at 35mm, pretty sharp at 50mm, a bit back focused again at 70mm (which is odd because it was also at 35mm, half this), but tack sharp from 100-300 in the center. The autofocus is not instant, so just be patient with it. Also I find that I get best results if I move the focus ring a bit before I autofocus. The lens is attractive and feels good in the hand, and having this kind of range on personal outings where I'm only shooting just for the fun of shooting (i.e. camping trips, visits to the park) I couldn't be happier. I wouldn't use this for professional shoots, I'll leave that to my other two dedicated 2.8 lenses, but for just all around shooting this is a great deal.

My advice - buy the Samsung, buy the Motorola, buy a Sony, buy an Asus, buy an LG, buy any other smart watch...but do NOT buy an Apple watch (without adding on their ridiculous insurance plan as well since they know their watch is going to break).

title: Just make it easier to set up and use.
text:
I am going with being a bit generous with three stars, mostly because I got a very good price on it.

Set up is convoluted. This will be the second home NAS on my network and by a long shot the hardest to get running. The enclosed documentation is literally one line of text repeated in several languages and some links. You need to download the PDF to get any more than diagrams of how to assemble the physical hardware.

The documentation refers to various LEDs and what they mean, but there is no diagram to tell you which is which. Power and activity indicators seem pretty obvious. others are not. It is shipped sans firmware, so going online to install it has to come first. And again, no documentation.

After jumping through endless hoops I did get it online finding at least half a dozen shared folders already set up. I only want storage space for my network. I contacted the company and they have threatened to void my warranty if I remove their folders from my NAS. Doing so does require hacking the firmware. But, why? I just want to store some data. I have far too many folders to deal with already and I am not happy with having to re-configure Samba manually to get there. Assuming that will work, there are no instructions on how to do it. I'm seriously close to returning it. If I hadn't had to wait nearly 16 hours to sync blank drives just to get up and running, I would.

Just give me an option of "I know what I'm doing, just give me one share" and I'd be happy. Or at least, provide instructions on how to do that.
I would even accept "you may need to re-install stock firmware before we will provide warranty service". But, "If you want to modify the nas to the way you want, you can do that. However, that will void the warranty.", seems a bit harsh and not customer friendly.

Intel Core i3 using onboard graphics, 8gb ram, low-power PSU, a 2.5" HDD and one SSD. No need for a graphics card or major cooling. The Cooler Master 130 was overkill, kinda loud, and certainly not pretty when the front fan got dusty.

This case is the complete antithesis to the Cooler Master case. It's small (way smaller!), has almost no features, and doesn't provide much/any allowance for cooling. But for my needs, it's perfect. And it's slick looking! It took me about an hour to install everything and it was very easy. This was a much easier build than my first go-around with the Cooler Master case. There is little flexibility with this case, meaning things go where they are supposed to go. 2 drives on the bottom, motherboard against one side, the PSU the other side, and that's it. Super easy. Adding a graphics card is possible, but things would get really tight.

I did install 2 40mm fans for air intake. The case supports up to 4 of these fans. There are no clips for cable management anywhere, so be careful with wires. I simply made sure nothing was up against the CPU fan.

I didn't have a problem with the screws (some report they are easily stripped). The case is very well-made with no sharp corners or anything. My one (rather small) gripe would involve the top & bottom panels. They would look nicer if they were chamfered a little. Instead they are a tad rough looking, but one has to look pretty close to notice. The power button blue LED looks nice and part of it flashed purple when the HDD is accessed. Overall, very pleased!

The sub is very clean looking, solidly built and has several nice features (multiple inputs, adjustable volume & cross-over, phase switch and standby mode). But the best thing about this speaker, as it should be, is the sound this thing produces. You can make it as loud as you want, but the value of a good sub is the reproduction of a rich, full, powerful sound at relatively low volume, This speaker does that with ease. I highly recommend this speaker.

title: finally found the one for me.
text:
It took me awhile to find the right sound bar for me.

I originally wanted to upgrade from my older Sony sound bar. I bought a new LG tv and figured an LG sound bar would go good with it so I went with a mid range sound bar, the LG SH7B. It was definitely an upgrade but not the best. I was happy enough with it until the sub started cutting out and I would have to unplug it multiple times a day to fix it. So I returned it and looked for something else.

I then searched for a sound bar made by an audio company instead of a tv company like LG or Samsung and found the Klipsch rsb-11 and it sounded great! I loved the sound. There was so much more detail coming from that sound bar that I have been missing with the other sound bars. The only issue was that I would hear a hiss/static noise coming from it in the evening when I had the volume lowered while my kids were sleeping. I couldn't hear it all the time just when it was quite but it was enough to annoy me. I tried a surge protector with "clean power" and other outlets as well as unplugging everything except the power cord. Nothing helped so I returned it and got another and that one did the same thing. I then went to my local Best Buy since they had it on display and that did it as well. I contacted Klipsch and they said it's normal. Now it is normal to hear noise from speakers when you are really close to them. But I would hear it sitting on my couch 10ft away, that's not normal.

I then bought the Polk Audio Magnifi Max and was very unhappy with the sound quality. There was more bass but it wasn't as nice sounding bass and it also just rolled right into the mids and lacked the highs. It was just very muddy sounding. There is no way I would be happy with that sound after listening to Klipsch so I was back to searching.

I finally came to this sound bar and am now satisfied. It may not sound as great as the Klipsch but it's very close. Great low, mids and highs with great clarity. If you want great sound without a full surround set up for a fair price then go with this, you'll be happy.

I am a long time Amazon customer. LONG TIME. I am becoming more and more dissatisfied with Amazon as a company. Over the years I have seen my 2 day prime shipping turn in to 4-5 days, with no or lame explanations as to why. Apparently suddenly there is a "processing time" that wasn't necessary up until recently. Then I've seen my calls to Amazon get routed overseas to the Philippines, so that more often than not, I can not understand the person I am talking to. And now I am seeing a decline in the trust I had put in products carrying the Amazon name. I currently own an Amazon Fire TV, the Amazon Fire TV game remote, 5 kindles, 4 kindle fires, and the Amazon Echo. I bought the fire tv to replace a very old roku box I had had so long it was a dinosaur. It still works! But it is past being able to receive updates. Therefore I ordered the matching Amazon Fire TV remote. That remote didn't last one year. It was a total piece of junk. Before long the A button started sticking to the point that it was unusable. Now, my Fire tv box is having issues. It randomly shuts down, and cannot be brought back to life without unplugging it and plugging it back in. After that, it works again, with the remote as it should. But up until it is unplugged, no amount of cajoling will bring it to life. But, this device comes with a 1 year warranty. And guess what? I am past that. So, basically it is trash. I think a device that costs $99 should last longer than a year. I might have considered replacing it with another, thinking maybe a I got a dud. But then another thing happened which I will not tolerate. Amazon has started sticking little commercial ads in front of shows. So for example, when I sit my littlest children down to watch an episode of Mister Rogers on Amazon Prime, the first thing that comes up after I select that show, is a commercial for an Amazon Prime Original series, meant for middle school children!! I am quite sure that middle school children are not watching Mister Rogers! And that content is NOT suitable for my 3 and 5 year olds. I am already paying an inflated amount yearly for my Amazon Prime "service". In addition to taking my money, must they also subject my family and I to commercials we have no desire to see?? Apparently. So of course I called, and after spending time I don't have trying to explain the problem to someone who speaks English as a SECOND language, I was told the problem was fixed. Well it isn't. In fact it is happening even more often now. One reason I do not have cable tv is because I do not want commercials blasted in to my home. And I don't appreciate them being piped in on my Amazon Fire tv device either. What has happened to you Amazon? I used to brag about you endlessly. I was totally thrilled with you as a company. Now? title: In my opinion, the best streaming device I've used....
text:
I was introduced to the Amazon Fire TV by purchasing one for my father last Christmas. He seemed to love it, so this year I decided to get one for myself....and I'm not disappointed. The new 4K features are too new for what my entertainment system can do for now, but the apps, games, and channels perform really well. The system itself is really responsive and fast (unlike a Roku I purchased months before...still can't figure that out. I mean...they're basically streaming devices...but the Roku performed less than expected on my Wi-Fi and road runner internet speeds. It locked up a lot too. A borrowed Chromecast to try out didn't do much better. Same internet...same wifi.) The Amazon just seems to perform better in every way.

I haven't used Alexa to the fullest yet, but what I have used has worked without any glitches. I mostly just use Alexa for playing content from my Amazon cloud music and such. All in all a really terrific, fast, responsive and intuitive unit that will certainly be getting a lot more use as time goes on.
If you're curious at all, I mostly use apps like HBO Now, Netflix, Youtube, Pandora, Smithsonian, PBS, Prime....etc...

My only complaint? Sometimes....only sometimes....I do get a little frustrated when I search for a movie, find the results, and wind up having to pay additional rental fees through Amazon Prime. It's a small complaint....I know that's how Prime is set up...but sometimes I feel that with the membership payment, a lot of movies I would like to watch you'd think would be included. Don't get me wrong, there are tons of free movies and tv....but....certain movies I would think would be free (something from 1993 or 1999 or whatever) still have rental fees. Again, it's just a small complaint...other than that, I love the Fire TV and all the apps and games that are at your fingertips. And I continue to discover more. Keep doing what you're doing Amazon, and you'll have something even better.

Oh....one small suggestion.....how about adding a feature to be able to plug-in an external hard-drive and watch content off of the drive through the Fire TV? Roku and another device does it....it's your turn! It would be a great addition to an already terrific machine.....I highly recommend the Fire TV.
